topics.title: Who You Are
topics.subtitle: Hebrew. Israel. Joint Heir With the King From Judah.
topics.lede: If He came back for a bride, who is she now? And what does that make you? The answer runs in four links, and every one of them is a verse you can go read yourself.
topics.note: All Scripture from the World English Bible Companion to The Marriage Covenant

blocks.v: The first teaching showed that YHWH married Israel at Sinai, divorced the northern house for her unfaithfulness, and then died in the flesh as Yahshua so He could lawfully take her back. Two sticks, one hand. This teaching answers the question that comes next. If He came back for a bride, who is she now? And what does that make you? YHWH is the Creator's name. Yahshua is the Hebrew name of the Messiah.

sections.heading: Hebrew Means One Who Crossed Over

blocks.v: Start with the word itself. The Hebrew word Ivri, which we say as "Hebrew," comes from the root avar, meaning to pass over, to cross over, to go through to the other side. The first man called by that name is Abraham:
"One who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew."
Why was he called that? Because of what he did:
"Your fathers lived of old time beyond the River... I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan."
He was on one side. YHWH called him. He left everything he knew, crossed over, and never went back. That is what the name means. Not a bloodline. A crossing. And that is exactly what happened to you:
"Most certainly I tell you, he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and doesn't come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life."
"...who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love."
Out of one thing. Into another. You crossed over.
Now, does that crossing actually make you family? Or are you standing outside watching someone else's inheritance? Scripture answers it directly, and it is not subtle:
"Know therefore that those who are of faith are children of Abraham."
"If you are Messiah's, then you are Abraham's offspring and heirs according to promise."
Notice how the promise was set up in the first place. Abraham was counted righteous before he was circumcised, so that the promise could reach people who came to YHWH the same way he did:

"...that he might be the father of all those who believe... For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace, to the end that the promise may be sure to all the offspring." Abraham is the father of everyone who crosses over the way he crossed over.
Paul takes it further. He does not say you get a separate arrangement alongside Israel. He says you are put into Israel:
"But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree..."
A graft is not a guest. A graft is fed by the root and becomes part of the tree.

"...you were at that time separate from Messiah, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise... But now in Messiah Yahshua you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Messiah."
Read that carefully. Alienated from the commonwealth. You cannot be alienated from something you were never part of. And now you are brought near, not introduced for the first time.
"So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and of the household of Elohim."
And this is not a new idea Paul invented. It was always the rule:

"You shall divide it by lot for an inheritance to you and to the aliens who live among you... they shall be to you as the native-born among the children of Israel. They shall have inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel."
"For they are not all Israel that are of Israel... it is not the children of the flesh who are children of Elohim, but the children of the promise are counted as heirs."

sections.heading: Judah, and What You Actually Are

blocks.v: Here is where people get this wrong in both directions, so let us be careful and let Scripture say exactly what it says. The King came from Judah. That much is plain:
"The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs."
"...Behold, the Lion who is of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome."
"For it is evident that our Master has sprung out of Judah."
And you are made a joint heir with Him. Not a servant of the household. An heir alongside the Son:

"...you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, 'Abba! Father!' The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of Elohim; and if children, then heirs: heirs of Elohim and joint heirs with Messiah."

Joint heir. Whatever belongs to the King from Judah, you inherit alongside Him. You live under that scepter. That is your King, that is your line, that is your inheritance. And inwardly, you are a Yehudi. Paul says this outright:

"For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly... but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter; whose praise is not from men, but from Elohim."
Now catch what Paul just did, because it is easy to read straight past. Yehudah, the name Judah, means praise. Leah gave him that name for that reason:
"She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, 'This time will I praise YHWH.' Therefore she named him Judah."

So when Paul defines the inward Jew and then ends the sentence with "whose praise is not from men, but from Elohim," he is not adding a nice closing thought. He is landing on the meaning of the name itself.
An inward Yehudi is one whose praise comes from YHWH.

sections.heading: One Thing to Be Careful About

blocks.v: You will hear people say "we are the tribe of Judah now." Be careful there, and here is why. In Scripture, tribe is reckoned through the father's house, by physical descent:
"They assembled all the congregation together... and they declared their ancestry after their families, by their fathers' houses."
More importantly, the whole two sticks prophecy depends on Judah and Israel staying two distinct houses that get joined:
"Behold, the days come," says YHWH, "that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah."

blocks.title: Why It Matters
blocks.v: If everyone simply becomes Judah, there is no second stick left to join, and the promise of Ezekiel 37 has nothing to fulfill.
So we do not need to claim the tribe. What Scripture actually gives is better, and it holds up under any question:

You crossed over, so you are Hebrew in the meaning of the word. You are Abraham's seed by faith. You are grafted into Israel and fed by her root. You are joint heir with the King who came from Judah, living under His scepter. You are a Yehudi inwardly, circumcised in the heart, whose praise comes from YHWH and not from men.
Nobody can take any of those from you, and none of them require a genealogy.

You are not a visitor at someone else's table. You are not a late addition to a story that belongs to another people. You were far off, and you were brought near by blood. You crossed over the way Abraham crossed over. You were grafted into the tree, you feed on the root, and you are an heir with the King.
"But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for Elohim's own possession... who in time past were no people, but now are Elohim's people."
Those words in 1 Peter come straight out of Exodus 19, the wedding proposal at Sinai. And "no people who are now His people" is Hosea, spoken over the divorced house.
The Husband died to get her back. And when He rose, He brought you home with her.

refIndex.topic: The King From Judah, And The Inward Yehudi

topics.title: The Marriage Covenant
topics.subtitle: Why Yahshua Had to Die to Get His Bride Back
topics.lede: Sinai was a wedding. The bride was unfaithful. She was lawfully divorced, and His own instruction barred her return. This is how He kept His word without breaking a single letter of it.
topics.note: All Scripture from the World English Bible Companion teaching: Who You Are

blocks.v: If some of this is new to you, these four will carry you through the whole teaching.

items: YHWH is the actual name of the Creator as it appears in the Hebrew Scriptures. Most Bibles replace it with the title "the LORD" in capital letters. We use His name.
Yahshua is the Hebrew name of the Messiah, the name most people know as Jesus.

Torah means "instructions." It is the first five books of the Bible. Think of it less as a rule book and more as terms and guidance given by a Husband to His bride. That will matter a great deal in a moment.

The two houses. After King Solomon died, the nation of Israel split in two. The northern kingdom kept the name Israel, sometimes called Ephraim or Joseph. The southern kingdom was called Judah, where we get the word "Jew." This split is not a small detail. It is the key to the whole story.

blocks.v: When YHWH brought Israel out of Egypt and met them at Mount Sinai, He was not simply handing down a legal code. He was proposing marriage. Read the scene with that in mind and it changes completely.
He makes the proposal:

"You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you to myself. Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples."
The bride answers:
"All the people answered together, and said, 'All that YHWH has spoken we will do.'"
That is the "I do."
Then she prepares herself. She washes her garments and waits three days, which is the bridal immersion.
"Go to the people, and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments, and be ready for the third day."
Then the covenant is sealed in blood, the way covenants were:
"Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, 'Look, this is the blood of the covenant, which YHWH has made with you concerning all these words.'"
And if there is any doubt about what just happened, YHWH says it Himself, plainly, centuries later:
"...which my covenant they broke, although I was a husband to them," says YHWH.
He says it again through Ezekiel, in language no one can mistake:
"Yes, I swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you," says the Lord YHWH, "and you became mine."

blocks.title: The Point
blocks.v: The Torah is the marriage contract. The instructions are the terms of the covenant a Husband gave to His wife.

The northern kingdom, Israel, turned to other gods. Scripture does not describe this as a policy failure or a religious mistake. It calls it adultery, because that is exactly what it is when a wife gives herself to another.
"...backsliding Israel had committed adultery..."

sections.heading: He Gave Her a Certificate of Divorce

blocks.v: This is the part most people have never been taught, and it changes everything:

"I saw, when, for this very cause that backsliding Israel had committed adultery, I had put her away and given her a bill of divorce, yet treacherous Judah her sister didn't fear; but she also went and played the prostitute."
Notice carefully who received the certificate. Israel, the northern house, was divorced. Judah was not. Judah watched it happen and did not learn from it, but Judah remained in covenant.

That single verse is the reason the two houses have had two different histories ever since. Judah kept the name, the identity, the Scriptures. Israel was scattered into the nations and lost all of it.
"Call his name Lo-Ammi; for you are not my people, and I will not be yours."
Lo-Ammi means "not my people." The divorced wife was sent out, absorbed into the nations, and forgot who she was.
Here is where it becomes remarkable.
YHWH promises to take her back:
"I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion."
But His own instruction forbids it. In the covenant terms He Himself gave, a man may not remarry the wife he divorced once she has been joined to another man:
"...her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before YHWH."
And she had been joined to another. She went after other gods. That is the whole reason she was sent away.
Now read this verse slowly, because YHWH raises the exact objection Himself:

"They say, 'If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him, and become another man's, should he return to her again?' Wouldn't that land be greatly polluted? But you have played the prostitute with many lovers; yet return again to me," says YHWH.
He names the legal obstacle, then says come back anyway.
So He has bound Himself two ways at once. He swore to take her back. His own righteous instruction says He cannot. And He does not break His word:
"I will not break my covenant, nor alter what my lips have uttered."
"For I, YHWH, don't change."

blocks.title: Hold This Tension
blocks.v: This is not a loophole to be found. It is a genuine problem, and there is only one thing in all of Scripture that resolves it.
There is exactly one event that releases a wife from her marriage covenant, and it is not divorce. It is death.
"For the woman that has a husband is bound by law to the husband while he lives, but if the husband dies, she is discharged from the law of the husband."
Paul is not making a side comment about marriage here. He is making this exact argument, and he says where it lands:

"Therefore, my brothers, you also were made dead to the law through the body of Messiah, that you would be joined to another, to him who was raised from the dead, that we might produce fruit to Elohim."
Joined to another. To Him who was raised from the dead.

The Husband died. Death ends the covenant, and when the covenant ends, the barrier of Deuteronomy 24 ends with it. She is no longer a divorced woman who cannot return. She is a widow, and a widow is free to marry.
"For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it. For a will is in force where there has been death."

And here is the piece that ties it together. The Husband was YHWH Himself. No one else's death could have done it, because no one else was the Husband. So He came in the flesh as Yahshua, and He died.
Then He rose, no longer bound by the former covenant, free to betroth her again without violating one word of His own instruction.
"For I married you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Messiah."

blocks.title: The Whole Teaching In One Sentence
blocks.v: The cross was not YHWH setting aside His own standard to make an exception. It was YHWH satisfying His own standard completely, at the cost of His own life, so He could keep His promise.
Now the prophecy in Ezekiel makes sense.

"...I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions; and I will put them with it, with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in my hand."
"...they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all."
Two sticks. Two houses. One divorced, one not. The resurrection is the legal act that makes their reunion possible, because the divorced one could not come home until the Husband died.
Watch who the renewed covenant is made with:
"Behold, the days come," says YHWH, "that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah."
Both houses. Named separately. Because only one of them needed the legal remedy, but both are brought into the same covenant.
And the ones who were called "not my people" get their identity back:
"...in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' they will be called 'sons of the living El.' Then the children of Judah and the children of Israel will be gathered together."
Paul says the same thing to people out in the nations:

"...you were at that time separate from Messiah, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise... But now in Messiah Yahshua you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Messiah."
Read that again. Not brought in as strangers. Brought near, back to a commonwealth they were alienated from. You cannot be alienated from something you never belonged to.
If you have ever felt like you were too far gone, that you had disqualified yourself, that whatever you did put you permanently outside of what YHWH would receive... this is your story.
She was unfaithful. She was legally divorced. She had gone to another. By the letter of the covenant she could never come home.
And He died to bring her back.
That is not YHWH lowering His standard for you. That is YHWH paying the full price of His own standard so that He could keep you.
"For your Maker is your husband; YHWH of Armies is his name."
And it ends where every wedding ends:
"Let us rejoice and be exceedingly glad, and let us give the glory to him. For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready."
"If His death freed her from the covenant, wouldn't that just leave her free, not remarried to Him?"

Yes, and that is exactly the point. She had to be freed first. As a divorced woman who had gone to another, she was permanently barred from returning. As a widow, she is free to marry anyone, including the One who rose. The death removed the barrier. The resurrection provided the Husband.
"Was Judah divorced too?"

No. Isaiah 50:1 asks, "Where is the bill of your mother's divorce?" and the answer is that there isn't one. That question is spoken to Zion, to Judah. Judah was never given a certificate. Only the northern house was, which is exactly why the two houses have to be brought back together.
"Did YHWH die?"

Yahshua is YHWH come in the flesh. He laid down His life and took it up again. This is why He and no one else could resolve it. Any other death would have been the death of someone who was not the Husband, and it would have changed nothing.
"So does this mean the instructions were cancelled?"

No. The opposite. The whole reason He had to die is that He would not set aside a single word of His own instruction. If the instructions could simply be waived, there would have been no need for a cross at all.

topics.title: Yahshua Is the Father
topics.subtitle: The Covenant, the Divorce, and the Redemption
topics.lede: A covenantal study of why the Husband of Israel had to come in the flesh, die, and rise in order to lawfully bring His bride home.

blocks.v: This is not a study about a doctrine. It is a study about a marriage.

Scripture does not present redemption as a legal transaction between strangers. It presents it as a husband recovering a wife who left him. Once you see the covenant as a marriage, the divorce as a real divorce, and the redemption as a lawful remarriage, the identity of Yahshua stops being an abstract debate and becomes the only thing that makes the story work.

Every reference in this study has been checked. Quotations follow the World English Bible, which is in the public domain, with the Name restored as YHWH, Elohim in place of God, Yahshua in place of Jesus, Messiah in place of Christ, and Torah or instructions in place of law. Read every passage in your own copy. Do not take this study's word for anything.

blocks.title: A Word On Tone
blocks.v: If you hold a different position on this, you are welcome here. This study makes its case from the text and it names its own hard passages instead of hiding them. Weigh it. Test it. Bring your objections. Truth does not need to be protected from questions.

sections.heading: The Roles YHWH Keeps for Himself Alone

blocks.v: Before Yahshua is ever mentioned, Scripture locks certain roles down as belonging to YHWH and to no one else. This is the foundation. If it does not hold, nothing after it holds.
YHWH is the Husband of Israel
"For your Maker is your husband; YHWH of Armies is his name. The Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer. He will be called the Elohim of the whole earth."
One verse, two titles, one person. Husband and Redeemer. Hold that together, because Part Six turns on it.
YHWH speaks of "my covenant which they broke, although I was a husband to them."
"I swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you, says the Lord YHWH, and you became mine."
"In that day, says YHWH, you will call me 'my husband,' and no longer call me 'my master.'"
See also Jeremiah 3:14, "for I am a husband to you."
YHWH is the only Savior
"I myself am YHWH. Besides me, there is no savior."
"you shall acknowledge no Elohim but me, and besides me there is no savior."
See also Isaiah 45:21, "a just El and a Savior. There is no one besides me."
YHWH is the only Redeemer, and He worked alone
"YHWH, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: 'I am YHWH, who makes all things; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself.'"
The Hebrew behind "by myself" is l'vadi. Alone. No helper. No second party. No agent standing beside Him. That single word does more work in this study than any other word in the Tanakh.
"You, YHWH, are our Father. Our Redeemer from everlasting is your name."
Father and Redeemer. Same sentence. Same being.
YHWH is the First and the Last
"This is what YHWH, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, YHWH of Armies, says: 'I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no Elohim.'"
See also Isaiah 41:4 and Isaiah 48:12.
YHWH will not share His glory
"I am YHWH. That is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to engraved images."
Repeated in Isaiah 48:11. Whatever else is true, the glory and worship that belong to YHWH cannot lawfully land on a created being. Remember that when you reach Part Four.

sections.heading: Every One of Those Roles Lands on Yahshua

blocks.v: Husband and Bridegroom

John 3:29, John the Immerser calls Yahshua the bridegroom and calls himself only the friend of the bridegroom. Matthew 9:15, Yahshua calls Himself the bridegroom. Ephesians 5:25 to 32, Messiah is the husband, the assembly is the bride, and Paul calls it a great mystery. 2 Corinthians 11:2, Paul betrothed the assembly to one husband, Messiah. Revelation 19:7 to 9, the marriage of the Lamb, the bride made ready, the marriage supper.

YHWH said He is the husband of Israel. If Yahshua is a different being who is also the husband of Israel, then Israel now has two husbands. That is not a mystery. That is a violation of the very instructions the Husband gave her.
Savior
"our great Elohim and Savior, Yahshua Messiah."

This is the strongest one grammatically. In the Greek a single article governs both nouns, a construction that describes one person, not two. The same construction appears in 2 Peter 1:1, "our Elohim and Savior, Yahshua Messiah."
"There is no other name under heaven that is given among men, by which we must be saved."
Redeemer

Galatians 3:13, "Messiah redeemed us from the curse of the Torah, having become a curse for us." Titus 2:14, "that he might redeem us from all lawlessness." Revelation 5:9, "you were killed, and bought us for Elohim with your blood." 1 Peter 1:18 to 19, redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Messiah. Acts 20:28, the assembly "which he purchased with his own blood."
First and Last

"I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever." Read those two sentences together. Isaiah 44:6 says the First and the Last is YHWH and there is no Elohim besides Him. Revelation 1:18 says that same First and Last died and came back. The one who cannot be anyone but YHWH is the one who went into the grave. That is this entire study in two verses.
See also Revelation 2:8 and Revelation 22:12 to 13, where verse 16 names the speaker as Yahshua.
The glory He said He would not share
"glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed."
Set that beside Isaiah 42:8. Either YHWH broke His own word, or the one asking is YHWH.

sections.heading: Where a YHWH Passage Is Applied Directly to Yahshua

blocks.v: This is the quiet part of the study, and it may be the strongest. Here the writers of the Renewed Covenant take a passage that is explicitly about YHWH and apply it to Yahshua without hesitation or explanation.

rows.v: Philippians 2:10 to 11

rows.v: John 19:37, Revelation 1:7

rows.v: 1 Peter 2:7 to 8, Romans 9:33
John 8:58, and they picked up stones
1 Corinthians 10:4 and 9, the Rock was Messiah

blocks.v: And then there is the verse that says it outright.
"For a child is born to us. A son is given to us; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty El, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace."
The child born is called Everlasting Father. Not a representative of the Father. Not an ambassador from the Father. Father.
Add Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23, Immanuel, El with us. And Zechariah 14:9, "YHWH will be one, and his name one."

sections.heading: The Visible Image of the Invisible

blocks.v: "He who has seen me has seen the Father... the Father who lives in me does his works."
Do not stop at the first half of that. The second half is the framework for everything else. The Son is the visible Man in whom the invisible Father dwells and works.

John 10:30, "I and the Father are one." John 12:45, "He who sees me sees him who sent me." Colossians 1:15, "the image of the invisible Elohim." Colossians 2:9, "in him all the fullness of the Deity dwells bodily." Hebrews 1:3, "the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance." John 1:1 and 14, the Word was Elohim, and the Word became flesh. Philippians 2:6 to 8, existing in the form of Elohim, He emptied Himself and took the form of a servant.
Worship that belongs to YHWH alone

Matthew 14:33, the disciples in the boat worship Him. Matthew 28:9 and 17, worship after the resurrection. John 20:28, Thomas says "My Master and my Elohim," and Yahshua does not correct him. John 5:23, "that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father." Hebrews 1:6, "Let all the angels of Elohim worship him." Revelation 5:13 to 14, every created thing gives blessing and honor and glory to the One on the throne and to the Lamb. forbids it, and no one stops it.

sections.heading: The Marriage, and Then the Divorce

blocks.v: You cannot understand a divorce until you have seen the wedding.
The marriage at Sinai

Exodus 19:5 to 8, the proposal and her answer, "All that YHWH has spoken we will do." Exodus 24:3 to 8, the covenant confirmed in blood at the foot of the mountain. Jeremiah 2:2, "I remember for you the kindness of your youth, the love of your betrothals; how you went after me in the wilderness." Ezekiel 16:8, "I entered into a covenant with you, and you became mine."

The instructions given at Sinai are the terms of that marriage. This is why the prophets never call idolatry a policy failure. They call it adultery and prostitution, every single time. See Jeremiah 3:6 to 9, Ezekiel 16:15 to 34, and Hosea 2:2 to 13.

It is also why the cup at the Passover table is betrothal language and not the founding of a new religion. Matthew 26:27 to 29, "I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father's Kingdom." That is a bridegroom's promise to return for the wedding.
The divorce

"I saw, when, for this very cause that backsliding Israel had committed adultery, I had put her away and given her a certificate of divorce, yet treacherous Judah her sister didn't fear; but she also went and played the prostitute."
Three details matter, and most teaching blurs all three.

The certificate went to the northern house, Israel, also called Ephraim. Not to Judah. Judah was never handed a certificate, yet Jeremiah 3:11 says she was worse. Isaiah 50:1 asks Judah directly, "Where is the bill of your mother's divorce, with which I have put her away?"
Both houses are broken. Only one of them is legally divorced. That distinction is why the restoration in Part Seven has to join two things back together and not simply repair one.
The northern house was then named Lo-Ruhamah, not shown mercy, and Lo-Ammi, not my people (Hosea 1:6 and 9), and scattered into the nations (2 Kings 17:6 to 23).

sections.heading: The Legal Problem, and the Only Lawful Answer

blocks.v: The instruction

A man puts his wife away with a certificate. She leaves and becomes another man's wife. If that second husband divorces her or dies, "her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife after she is defiled; for that is abomination before YHWH."
The bar is specific. It falls on the first husband, and it takes effect after she has belonged to another.
Jeremiah raises the problem himself

"They say, 'If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man's, should he return to her again?' Wouldn't that land be greatly polluted? But you have played the prostitute with many lovers; yet return again to me, says YHWH."
Read that slowly. YHWH quotes His own instruction. He acknowledges that it forbids the very thing He is about to do. And then He calls her home anyway, without yet explaining how.
That unexplained answer is the whole point of this study.
Stating the problem correctly
The question was never how the marriage ended. The covenant breaking and the certificate ended it. Jeremiah 3:8 says so plainly.

The question is how He can ever lawfully receive her back, when His own instruction bars the first husband from taking back a wife who has belonged to another, and when Isaiah 42:8 tells us He does not set His own standard aside to get what He wants.
The second lock on the same door

There is a second requirement, and it is even harder than the first. In Scripture the one who buys back a lost inheritance or a lost person is the go'el, the kinsman redeemer. The requirements are laid out in Leviticus 25:25 and 47 to 49, and acted out in the book of Ruth.
He must be a near kinsman, an actual blood relation. He must be able to pay the full price. He must be willing to pay it. He must be free himself, not in the same bondage.
"None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give Elohim a ransom for him, for the redemption of their life is costly."
Now put the constraints side by side.

rows.topic: No one but YHWH is Redeemer (Isaiah 44:24, 43:11)
rows.v: Rules out every created being

rows.topic: YHWH stretched out the heavens alone, by Himself (Isaiah 44:24)
rows.v: Rules out an agent acting on His behalf

blocks.v: The lawful path home
With both locks in view, the sequence is not mysterious. It is the only sequence available.

The first husband dies. The bar of Deuteronomy 24:4 attaches to a living former husband. A dead man is not a first husband taking anyone back. He rises. Not as the former husband reclaiming a defiled wife, but as the living one, free to enter a new covenant with her.
The covenant that follows is stated to be new, not the old one patched. This is exactly what was promised.

"Behold, the days come, says YHWH, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers... which covenant of mine they broke, although I was a husband to them."
That is the answer to Jeremiah 3:1. And notice who it is made with. Both houses.

Paul reaches for the same principle in Romans 7:1 to 4, that death dissolves a binding obligation. He is drawing an illustration, not writing marriage legislation, so use it the way he used it. The principle holds either way. Death ends the binding.
The picture acted out in advance
YHWH tells Hosea to go and love an adulterous wife again, and Hosea buys her back for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of barley.
The husband pays a purchase price to recover the wife who went to another. Centuries later, in the same language: Revelation 5:9, "you bought us for Elohim with your blood."
Hosea is the answer key handed to us long before the exam.
The bride being gathered is not a replacement for Israel and never was. She is the divorced wife brought home from the nations and joined again to her sister.

Hosea 1:10 to 11, in the place where it was said "you are not my people," they will be called sons of the living El, and the children of Judah and the children of Israel will be gathered together under one head. Hosea 2:23, "I will say to those who were not my people, 'You are my people.'" Romans 9:24 to 26, Paul quotes Hosea and applies it to those called from among the nations. 1 Peter 1:1 with 2:9 to 10, written to the scattered, "who in time past were no people, but now are Elohim's people." James 1:1, "to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion." Ezekiel 37:15 to 28, the two sticks become one in His hand, one king over them, an everlasting covenant, His dwelling among them. John 10:16, "I have other sheep, which are not of this fold... they will become one flock with one shepherd." John 11:51 to 52, He would die "that he might also gather together into one the children of Elohim who are scattered abroad." Ephesians 2:11 to 19, those once far off and alienated from the commonwealth of Israel are brought near, the dividing wall broken down, the two made one new man. Romans 11:17 to 24, grafted into the olive tree, with a warning not to boast against the branches. Isaiah 54:1 to 8, the forsaken wife called back: "For a small moment I have forsaken you; but with great mercies I will gather you."
Revelation 21:12 to 14 shows the finished bride as a city with the twelve tribes written on her gates and the twelve emissaries on her foundations. Both houses. One city. One bride.
A teaching that hides its difficult passages does not deserve to be believed. Here are the strongest objections and the most honest answers this study can give.
"He prayed to the Father. Who was He talking to?"

John 17, Matthew 26:39, Hebrews 5:7. The flesh is real, not theater. Philippians 2:7 says He emptied Himself and took the form of a servant. John 14:10 gives the framework in His own words, "the Father who lives in me does his works." A man genuinely praying is exactly what an incarnation looks like. This objection carries real weight and should never be waved off. Scripture calls this the mystery of godliness (1 Timothy 3:16) and asserts it far more than it explains it.
"The Father is greater than I." John 14:28

Read the whole verse and its setting. He speaks of going to the Father, in the emptied state of Philippians 2:7. Then set it beside John 10:30, "I and the Father are one," which came out of the same mouth in the same ministry.
"Not even the Son knows the day." Mark 13:32
The self limiting is real and Philippians 2:7 names it. This is a statement about the Son in the flesh, not about the eternal Spirit who fills Him.
"He sits at the right hand." Psalm 110:1, Acts 7:55 to 56

The right hand is a Hebrew idiom for the position of power, not a second chair. Exodus 15:6, "Your right hand, YHWH, is glorious in power." Revelation 22:1 and 3 speak of "the throne of Elohim and of the Lamb," one throne. Even so, Stephen sees two distinct things, and honesty requires saying that this is a hard passage. A vision shows the seer what he is able to bear.
"One mediator, the man Messiah Yahshua." 1 Timothy 2:5
Note the word man. The mediation happens through the flesh. The same letter speaks of Elohim manifested in the flesh. The Mediator is the Man in whom the fullness dwells bodily.
"The Word was with Elohim." John 1:1
The same verse ends "and the Word was Elohim." Whatever "with" carries, it cannot mean a second Elohim, because John 1:3 says all things were made through Him and Isaiah 44:24 says YHWH did it alone.
"Isaiah 44:6 mentions YHWH and His Redeemer separately."

The King of Israel and His Redeemer stand in apposition, two titles of the one speaker, which is why the sentence continues in the singular, "I am the first, and I am the last." Isaiah 44:24 does the same thing with Redeemer and Maker, and then says He acted alone.
Two verses this study will not lean on

Some teachers quote Luke 2:11 as "Messiah YHWH." The Greek reads Christos Kyrios, Messiah the Master, and no manuscript carries the Name there. It is a translator's choice, so it is offered here as an echo and never as proof. Others quote 1 Timothy 3:16 as "Elohim was manifested in the flesh." The older Greek manuscripts read "he who was manifested," a difference of two small marks inside one letter, and scholars are genuinely divided. Colossians 2:9 makes the same point with no dispute at all. A case this strong does not need contested verses, and refusing to use them is part of walking in truth.

sections.heading: The Whole Thing in One Page

blocks.v: If Yahshua is not YHWH:

Israel has two husbands, which her own covenant terms forbid. A second savior exists, after YHWH said there is none besides Him. A second redeemer exists, after YHWH said He acted alone. A created being receives the worship and the glory YHWH said He would not share. The divorce of Jeremiah 3 stands forever, because the first husband can never lawfully take her back. There is no wedding, because the Bridegroom is not the Husband she was married to.
But because Yahshua is the Father in the flesh:

The Husband became the kinsman, satisfying both locks on the door. The Husband paid the redemption price no man could pay. The Husband died, and death ends the binding. The Husband rose, free to make a covenant that is new and not the old one patched. The scattered house is called back and joined to Judah under one King. The Bridegroom is coming for a bride He is lawfully entitled to claim.

"I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever." Revelation 1:17 to 18. The One who cannot be anyone but YHWH is the One who went into the grave for His wife.

The exclusive roles of YHWH: Deuteronomy 6:4; Isaiah 41:4; 42:8; 43:11; 44:6; 44:24; 45:21 to 23; 48:11 to 12; 54:5; 63:16; Hosea 13:4; Zechariah 14:9 The marriage covenant: Exodus 19:5 to 8; 24:3 to 8; Jeremiah 2:2; 3:14; 31:32; Ezekiel 16:8; Hosea 2:16; Matthew 26:27 to 29 The divorce: Deuteronomy 24:1 to 4; 2 Kings 17:6 to 23; Isaiah 50:1; Jeremiah 3:1; 3:6 to 11; Ezekiel 16:15 to 34; Hosea 1:6 to 9; 2:2 to 13 The redemption mechanism: Leviticus 25:25, 47 to 49; Ruth 4:1 to 10; Psalm 49:7 to 8; Jeremiah 31:31 to 34; Hosea 3:1 to 3; Romans 7:1 to 4; Hebrews 2:14 to 17 Yahshua as Husband and Bridegroom: Matthew 9:15; 25:1 to 10; John 3:29; 2 Corinthians 11:2; Ephesians 5:25 to 32; Revelation 19:7 to 9 Yahshua as Savior and Redeemer: Acts 4:12; 20:28; Galatians 3:13; Titus 2:13 to 14; 2 Peter 1:1; 1 Peter 1:18 to 19; Revelation 5:9 Yahshua as First and Last: Revelation 1:17 to 18; 2:8; 22:12 to 13 and 16 YHWH passages applied to Yahshua: Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23; Isaiah 8:13 to 14 with 1 Peter 2:7 to 8 and Romans 9:33; Isaiah 9:6; Isaiah 40:3 with Matthew 3:3; Isaiah 45:23 with Philippians 2:10 to 11; Joel 2:32 with Romans 10:9 to 13; Malachi 3:1 with Mark 1:2; Zechariah 12:10 with John 19:37; Psalm 102:25 to 27 with Hebrews 1:10 to 12; Exodus 3:14 with John 8:58; 1 Corinthians 10:4 and 9 Fullness and image: John 1:1 and 14; 10:30; 12:45; 14:7 to 10; 17:5; Colossians 1:15; 2:9; Philippians 2:6 to 8; Hebrews 1:3 Worship: Matthew 14:33; 28:9 and 17; John 5:23; 20:28; Acts 10:25 to 26; 14:11 to 15; Hebrews 1:6; Revelation 5:13 to 14; 19:10; 22:8 to 9 Two houses restored: Isaiah 54:1 to 8; Jeremiah 31:31 to 34; Ezekiel 37:15 to 28; Hosea 1:10 to 11; 2:23; John 10:16; 11:51 to 52; Romans 9:24 to 26; 11:17 to 24; Ephesians 2:11 to 19; James 1:1; 1 Peter 1:1; 2:9 to 10; Revelation 21:12 to 14 Passages to study on the other side: John 1:1; 14:28; 17:1 to 26; Mark 13:32; Matthew 26:39; Psalm 110:1; Acts 7:55 to 56; 1 Corinthians 15:24 to 28; 1 Timothy 2:5; Hebrews 5:7

topics.title: The Aleph and the Tav
topics.subtitle: Yahshua the Creator, the Almighty, the First and the Last
topics.lede: A study of the titles Yahshua claims in Revelation, where those titles come from in the Prophets, and why only One Being can lawfully hold them.

blocks.v: Revelation does not end with a doctrine. It ends with a Name, and with a title that only one Being in all of Scripture is permitted to carry.

In the last chapter of the Bible, Yahshua says of Himself: "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End." Four verses later He signs His own name to it. That sentence is not a poetic flourish. It is a direct quotation of a self-description that YHWH gave through Isaiah seven hundred years earlier, in a sentence that specifically rules out anyone else holding it.

This study follows that one thread all the way down. Where the title comes from. What it means in Hebrew. What it demands about the identity of the One who speaks it. And how the rest of Scripture confirms the same conclusion from a completely different direction, through the passages that name Yahshua as the Creator of everything that exists.

Quotations follow the World English Bible, which is in the public domain, with the Name restored as YHWH, Elohim in place of God, Yahshua in place of Jesus, Messiah in place of Christ, and Torah or instructions in place of law. Read every passage in your own copy. Do not take this study's word for anything.

blocks.title: A Word On Tone
blocks.v: This study names its own weak arguments and hands you the objections before anyone else can. That is deliberate. A case this strong does not need a single stretched verse, and refusing to stretch them is part of walking in truth.

sections.heading: The Three Titles, and Who Speaks Them

blocks.v: Three titles run through Revelation in parallel. Track who says each one, and watch what happens by the end of the book.
Title Where it appears
Revelation 1:8; 21:6; 22:13
Revelation 1:17; 2:8; 22:13
Revelation 21:6; 22:13
The opening declaration
"I am the Alpha and the Omega," says YHWH Elohim, "who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty."
Notice what is stacked into one verse. The title, the eternal existence, the coming, and the Almighty. Hold all four together, because they show up again on other lips before the book is over.
Nine verses later, the same title, and a grave
"Don't be afraid. I am the first and the last, and the Living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever."
There is no ambiguity here at all. The speaker has scars. He walked out of a tomb. And He introduces Himself with the divine title.
"The first and the last, who was dead, and has come to life says these things."
The One on the throne
"It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End... He who overcomes, I will give him these things. I will be his Elohim, and he will be my son."
And then the book signs its own name
"Behold, I come quickly. My reward is with me, to repay to each man according to his work. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End."

"I, Yahshua, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies." Revelation 22:13 stacks all three titles into a single sentence, and three verses later the speaker gives His name. Every title that opened the book on the lips of YHWH Elohim the Almighty closes the book on the lips of Yahshua. The book never explains the overlap, never apologizes for it, and never treats it as a problem. It simply assumes what this study is about to prove.

blocks.title: Be Honest About This One
blocks.v: Some translations, following the later manuscript tradition, also place "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last" in Revelation 1:11. The oldest manuscripts do not have that phrase there, which is why many modern translations omit it. Do not build on 1:11. You do not need it. Revelation 1:17 and 22:13 with 22:16 carry the entire argument on their own, and refusing to use a disputed verse costs you nothing while it buys you enormous credibility.
John writes to assemblies who read Greek, so he gives the title in Greek letters. But John is a Hebrew man thinking Hebrew thoughts, and the expression he is translating is a Hebrew one.
Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet. Omega is the last. In Hebrew those positions belong to א aleph and ת tav.

Naming the first and last letters of the alphabet is a Hebrew way of saying the whole of it, end to end, with nothing left out. Everything that can be spelled, everything that can be spoken, everything that can be said, is contained between those two letters. To claim them is to claim the entirety.

"Alpha and Omega" is the translation. Aleph and Tav is the thought underneath it. And unlike Greek, Hebrew has an actual word spelled aleph-tav, תא, which appears in the very first verse of Scripture. Part Six deals with that, carefully and honestly.

sections.heading: Isaiah, and Where the Title Comes From

blocks.v: Yahshua is not inventing a phrase in Revelation. He is picking up a signature that YHWH had already stamped on Himself through the prophet, in language that deliberately shuts the door on anyone else using it.
"This is what YHWH, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, YHWH of Armies, says: 'I am the first, and I am the last; and besides me there is no Elohim.'"
"Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, YHWH, the first, and with the last, I am he."
"Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel my called: I am he. I am the first. I am also the last."
In Hebrew the phrase is ani rishon va'ani acharon. I am first, and I am last.

This is not a description of a role. It is an exclusive claim, and Isaiah 44:6 attaches the exclusion clause to it in the very same breath: besides me there is no Elohim. There is no room left in that sentence for a second holder of the title.

So there are only two possibilities. Either Isaiah was wrong when he said no one else can carry that name, or the One who carries it in Revelation 1:17 and 22:13 is YHWH Himself. There is no third option available, and this is the cleanest form of the argument you will ever preach. Do not complicate it.

sections.heading: The First and the Last Is the Creator

blocks.v: Now the two halves of this study meet. Isaiah does not leave "the First and the Last" floating as an abstract title. He ties it directly to the act of creation, in the same paragraph.
"I am he. I am the first. I am also the last. Yes, my hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand has spread out the heavens."
Read that as one sentence, because that is what it is. The First and the Last is the One whose hand laid the foundation of the earth. The title and the act belong to the same Person.
And then Isaiah closes off the one escape route a person might reach for, which is the idea that YHWH created through some other being acting on His behalf.
"YHWH, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: 'I am YHWH, who makes all things; who alone stretches out the heavens; who spreads out the earth by myself.'"

The Hebrew behind "by myself" is l'vadi. Alone. No helper, no assistant, no second party, no agent standing beside Him. Whatever else is true about creation, Isaiah forecloses the possibility that YHWH delegated it.
Now read what the emissaries say about Yahshua
"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim, and the Word was Elohim... All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made."

"For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, things visible and things invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him. He is before all things, and in him all things are held together."
"You, Master, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands. They will perish, but you continue... you are the same. Your years will not fail."

Hebrews 1:10 is quoting Psalm 102:25 to 27, a psalm addressed by name to YHWH the Creator. The writer of Hebrews takes those words and tells us the Father speaks them to the Son. That is not an inference drawn by this study. That is the plain claim of the text.
Add 1 Corinthians 8:6, one Elohim the Father of whom are all things, and one Master Yahshua Messiah through whom are all things.
