The apostles and the Sabbath: Acts 13:14, 42-44; Acts 17:2; Acts 18:4 Keeping it: Nehemiah 10:31; Nehemiah 13:15-22; Isaiah 58:13; Matthew 12:12; Leviticus 23:32; Mark 1:32 Never changed: Matthew 5:17-18; Isaiah 66:22-23; Acts 2:46; Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2 Common objections: Colossians 2:16-23; Romans 14:1-6; Galatians 4:8-10 Deliverance and forgiveness: Isaiah 58:6; Luke 13:16; Ephesians 4:26-27, 31-32; Matthew 6:14-15; James 4:6

topics.title: The Seven Feasts of YHWH
topics.subtitle: His appointed times, the shadow they cast, and the fulfillment in Yahshua
topics.note: A Kingdom Life teaching handout on Leviticus 23 Scripture from the World English Bible, divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Seven lamps stand on one lampstand, hammered out of a single piece of gold. Seven feasts stand on one calendar, hammered out of a single plan of redemption. They are not Jewish holidays and they are not ours to move. Leviticus 23 calls them the set feasts of YHWH, his appointed times, and Scripture shows him filling them in with real events on the exact days. The first four are already fulfilled. The last three are still ahead. If you want to know what YHWH is doing on the earth, he wrote the schedule down and told his people to keep it.

sections.heading: They Are His Feasts, Not Ours

blocks.v: Before Leviticus 23 lists a single date, it settles a question of ownership. Verse 2 names them twice and verse 4 names them again, and one of those is YHWH himself saying these are my appointed times. They do not belong to a nation, a denomination, or a culture. They belong to YHWH, and he is the one who assigns the calendar.
YHWH spoke to Moses, saying, “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘The set feasts of YHWH, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my set feasts.’”
These are the set feasts of YHWH, even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed season.

The Hebrew word behind set feast is moed, an appointed time, a fixed meeting. A moed is not a party. It is an appointment that one party has already put on the calendar and the other party is expected to keep.

The word behind holy convocation is miqra qodesh. Miqra comes from the root qara, to call, to proclaim, to summon, to read. It means a sacred assembly, a called gathering, a day his people are summoned to. It is worth saying plainly that it does not mean rehearsal. That is a popular teaching and it is not what the word carries. The prophetic weight of these days is real, but it comes from the events Scripture records landing on them, not from a meaning pressed into a Hebrew noun.

blocks.title: A Note On The Word Feast
blocks.v: Scripture itself uses two different words. Moed is the appointed time, and that is the word covering everything in Leviticus 23. Chag is the pilgrimage festival, and only three of these carry it: Unleavened Bread, Weeks, and Booths (Exodus 23:14-17; Deuteronomy 16:16). Calling all of them feasts is common English shorthand, and counting them as seven is a grouping we make rather than a number the chapter gives, since Leviticus 23 opens with the weekly Sabbath and closes with the eighth day assembly. Nothing in this study depends on the number. It depends on the chapter.
The appointments were built into creation itself before there was an Israel to keep them.
Elohim said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years.”
He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.

The word rendered seasons in both places is that same word, moed. The sun and moon were hung in the sky as the clock for his appointed times. That is why the feasts move on our modern calendar and never move on his.

blocks.title: Note The Wording
blocks.v: Four separate times in this one chapter these instructions are sealed with the phrase a statute forever throughout your generations (Leviticus 23:14, 21, 31, 41). Forever is a long time. Nothing in Scripture ever cancels these appointments, and the last book of the Bible still has the nations keeping one of them (Zechariah 14:16).

The picture of seven feasts standing on a menorah is a good one, because the menorah itself teaches the same lesson. It was not assembled from seven separate parts bolted together. It was beaten out of one solid piece of gold.

You shall make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand shall be made of hammered work. Its base, its shaft, its cups, its buds, and its flowers shall be of one piece with it. There shall be six branches going out of its sides.

One piece, one hammering, seven lights. The feasts are the same. They are not seven unrelated holidays. They are one plan, struck out of one mind, and each lamp throws light on the next one. Zechariah sees the same lampstand and is told plainly that it is not accomplished by might or power but by his Spirit (Zechariah 4:2, 6), and John sees Yahshua standing in the middle of seven lampstands in Revelation 1:12-13, 20.
A few things worth seeing before we walk the seven:

items: 1. The weekly Sabbath is listed first. Before Passover is mentioned, Leviticus 23:3 puts the seventh day Sabbath at the head of the list of appointed times. The yearly appointments are built on top of a weekly one that YHWH set at creation.

2. Three of them require a journey. Unleavened Bread, Weeks, and Tabernacles are the three times a year all the males were to appear before YHWH (Exodus 23:14-17; Deuteronomy 16:16). Those three anchor the spring, the summer, and the fall.

3. They fall in two clusters with a hinge in the middle. Four in the spring, in the first and third months. Three in the fall, all in the seventh month. Pentecost sits in the center of the lampstand, on the main shaft, joining the two.

4. The spring feasts are already fulfilled, to the day. Yahshua died at Passover, lay in the grave through Unleavened Bread, rose on Firstfruits, and poured out his Spirit on Pentecost. Not one of those was close to the date. Each was exact. That precision is the reason to take the three fall feasts seriously.

blocks.v: First month, 14th day, at twilight. Leviticus 23:5. The lamb slain and the blood applied.
First month, 15th through 21st, seven days. Leviticus 23:6-8. Sin removed and the body in the tomb.
The morrow after the Sabbath, Leviticus 23:11. The first sheaf lifted up, the resurrection.
Fifty days later, counted. Leviticus 23:15-22. Instructions at Sinai, the Spirit in Acts 2, written on hearts.
Seventh month, first day. Leviticus 23:23-25. A memorial of blowing, the only moed on the head of a month.
Seventh month, tenth day. Leviticus 23:26-32. Affliction, repentance, blood behind the veil.
Seventh month, 15th through 21st, plus the eighth day. Leviticus 23:33-43. Elohim dwelling with his people.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, is YHWH's Passover.

The instruction. Exodus 12 gives the whole picture. A lamb is selected on the tenth day, kept until the fourteenth, then killed at twilight by the whole assembly. The blood goes on the two doorposts and the lintel. The household eats the lamb inside the house, and death passes over every door where the blood is applied.

Your lamb shall be without defect, a male a year old. … The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you.

What it pictures. Substitution. The lamb dies in the place of the firstborn. Notice that the blood on the doorpost saved nobody who left it in the basin. Applied blood, not available blood, is what death passes over.
The fulfillment. Yahshua is the lamb. John the Immerser names him as such the first time he lays eyes on him.
“Behold, the Lamb of Elohim, who takes away the sin of the world!”
Purge out the old yeast, that you may be a new lump … For indeed Messiah, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place.

He was inspected publicly for days in Jerusalem and no fault was found (Luke 23:4, 14-15; John 18:38). The lamb was to have no bone broken (Exodus 12:46; Numbers 9:12; Psalm 34:20), and the soldiers who came to break his legs found him already dead and did not break one (John 19:33, 36). He was without blemish in the only way that counts (Isaiah 53:7, 9; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 4:15; 1 Peter 1:18-19).

blocks.title: On The Chronology
blocks.v: Yahshua shared a final meal with his disciples on the night he was betrayed (1 Corinthians 11:23). Matthew, Mark, and Luke call it the Passover (Matthew 26:17-20; Mark 14:12-17; Luke 22:7-15). John sets that evening before the feast of the Passover (John 13:1) and records that the next morning the leaders who handed him over still had not eaten the Passover (John 18:28). He was crucified on the Preparation Day, and John calls the Sabbath that followed a special one (John 19:14, 31), which fits a week carrying two Sabbaths. This study reads the meal as coming before the Passover the leaders kept. It does not claim he died at the same hour the lambs were slaughtered. Scripture does not say that.

blocks.title: The Doorpost Is Still The Question
blocks.v: Redemption has never been automatic. Egypt was full of lambs that night, but only the houses with blood on the door were passed over. The question was never whether the lamb was good enough. It was whether the blood had been applied to that particular door. Hebrews 9:22 puts it plainly: apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.

On the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread to YHWH. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. In the first day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.

The instruction. Seven days of bread with no leaven in it, and leaven put out of the houses entirely (Exodus 12:15-20; Exodus 13:6-7). Israel left Egypt in such a hurry the dough had no time to rise (Exodus 12:39). Deliverance was immediate, and there was no time to bring the old life along.
What it pictures. Leaven is the picture of sin working quietly through a whole life, and of corrupt teaching working through a whole assembly.

Your boasting is not good. Don't you know that a little yeast leavens the whole lump? … Therefore let's keep the feast, not with old yeast, neither with the yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

Paul writes that to a mixed assembly, long after the resurrection, and tells them to keep the feast. Yahshua used the same picture for doctrine, warning about the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which he explained was their teaching (Matthew 16:6-12).
The fulfillment. This is the feast of the burial. The sinless one, the bread without corruption in it, was laid in the tomb while the feast was being kept.
For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.

Peter and Paul both preach that verse as the resurrection proof: his flesh did not decay (Acts 2:27, 31; Acts 13:35-37). He called himself the bread of life that came down out of heaven, and said the bread he would give is his flesh (John 6:35, 48-51). He was born in Bethlehem, which means house of bread (Micah 5:2), and he was laid in a feeding trough.

Walking it out. Cleaning the leaven out of the house for a week is a physical picture of something spiritual. You go through cabinets you have not opened in a year and find things you forgot were there. That is the point.

When you have come into the land which I give to you, and shall reap its harvest, then you shall bring the sheaf of the first fruits of your harvest to the priest. He shall wave the sheaf before YHWH, to be accepted for you. On the next day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.

The instruction. The first sheaf of the barley harvest is cut and lifted up before YHWH, and nothing of the new harvest may be eaten until that sheaf is accepted (Leviticus 23:14). The first one presented guarantees that the whole field is coming.

Read the wording carefully. Leviticus 23:11 does not say the day after Unleavened Bread begins. It says the morrow after the Sabbath, and the count to Pentecost is measured from that same morrow through seven complete Sabbaths (Leviticus 23:15-16). This handout takes the Sabbath there as the weekly Sabbath, which is what the text says, rather than reading a later calendar system back into it.
The fulfillment. Paul does not hint at this. He names it.
But now Messiah has been raised from the dead. He became the first fruits of those who are asleep. … But each in his own order: Messiah the first fruits, then those who are Messiah's at his coming.

The women came to the tomb early on the first day of the week and found it already empty (Matthew 28:1-6; Mark 16:2-6; John 20:1). He is called the firstborn from the dead and the firstborn among many brothers (Colossians 1:18; Romans 8:29), and we are called a kind of firstfruits of his creatures (James 1:18). The wave sheaf had to be presented before anyone could eat, and on that morning Yahshua told Miriam not to hold him because he had not yet ascended to the Father (John 20:17). The sheaf was on its way to be presented.

blocks.title: On The Timing
blocks.v: He said the only sign given would be Jonah: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth (Matthew 12:40). A Wednesday evening burial, with the high Sabbath of Unleavened Bread following (John 19:31 calls it a great day, not the weekly one), gives exactly three days and three nights and still has the tomb empty before the women arrive on the first day. That week had two Sabbaths in it, which is why the accounts fit together rather than contradicting.

There was even a first harvest that came up with him: tombs were opened, and after his resurrection many bodies of holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised and appeared to many in the city (Matthew 27:52-53). A sheaf, not a single stalk.

You shall count from the next day after the Sabbath … seven Sabbaths shall be completed. Next day after the seventh Sabbath you shall count fifty days, and you shall offer a new meal offering to YHWH. … They shall be baked with yeast, for first fruits to YHWH.

The instruction. This is the only feast you have to count to. Fifty days from the wave sheaf, then two loaves of wheat bread are waved before YHWH, and these two loaves are deliberately baked with leaven, the only such offering in the chapter. The same passage ends by telling the farmer not to reap the corners of his field, but to leave the gleanings for the poor and the foreigner (Leviticus 23:22; compare Deuteronomy 16:9-12).

What it pictures at Sinai. Israel came to Sinai in the third month (Exodus 19:1). The mountain burned with fire, there was a voice like a trumpet, and YHWH spoke his instructions and wrote them with his own finger on stone (Exodus 19:16-20; 20:1-17; 31:18). Fire, a loud voice, and his words given to a gathered people. Hold that picture.
The fulfillment in Acts 2. The same feast, fire again, a sound from heaven again, and his instructions delivered again, this time not onto stone.

Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place. Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind … Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.
I will put my law in their inward parts, and I will write it in their heart. I will be their Elohim, and they shall be my people.

That is the whole point of the day. At Sinai his instructions went onto tablets of stone. In Acts 2 the same instructions went into hearts of flesh, exactly as Ezekiel 36:26-27 promised: a new heart, a new spirit, and his Spirit causing his people to walk in his statutes. Paul makes the comparison directly, saying we are a letter written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living Elohim, not on stone but on tablets that are hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3). Peter stood up and quoted Joel 2:28-29 to explain what everyone was watching (Acts 2:16-21).

There is a sober detail in the comparison. At Sinai, when the people made the calf, about three thousand men fell (Exodus 32:28). In Acts 2, about three thousand souls were added (Acts 2:41). The same number, running the other direction.

blocks.title: Why Two Loaves, And Why With Leaven
blocks.v: Every other offering in Leviticus 23 is unleavened. These two are not, and there are two of them. Leaven still pictures what is in us, so these loaves read as a picture of a people accepted and waved before him while they are still being dealt with. Two of them, waved together as one offering, lines up with the two sticks of Ezekiel 37:15-22 becoming one in his hand, and with the two being made into one new man in Ephesians 2:11-16. Judah and Ephraim, the near and the far off, lifted up together. Leviticus does not spell that out, so take it as a pattern worth weighing rather than a commandment.

The gleaning instruction attached to this feast is not decoration either. It is the instruction that put Ruth, a Moabite, in the field of Boaz between the barley and the wheat harvests (Ruth 1:22; 2:2-3, 23). A foreigner gleaning at Pentecost, redeemed by a kinsman, and written into the line of the Messiah.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, shall be a solemn rest to you, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.

The instruction. A day of blowing, on the first day of the seventh month (Numbers 29:1-6). The trumpets themselves were given for gathering the assembly, for setting out on a journey, for sounding an alarm in war, and for the appointed times and new moons (Numbers 10:1-10; Psalm 81:3).

What makes this one different. It is the only appointed time in Leviticus 23 that falls on the head of a month. Every other one is counted from a date already fixed inside a month that is already running. This one begins when the month begins.

blocks.title: Say Only What Torah Says
blocks.v: It is common to teach that this day waits on a crescent sighting. This handout does not, because Torah gives no such commandment. There is no verse instructing anyone to go out, look for a first visible crescent, and declare the month on the testimony of witnesses. What Scripture does say is that the moon was appointed for the moedim (Psalm 104:19) and that trumpets sounded at the beginnings of the months (Numbers 10:10; Numbers 28:11). The month is tied to the moon. The mechanism is not spelled out, and 1 Samuel 20:5, 18 shows David and Jonathan knowing the day in advance. Where Scripture stops speaking, we stop calling our interpretation a commandment.
The fulfillment ahead. Every passage about his return has a trumpet in it.

For Adonai himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel and with Elohim's trumpet. The dead in Messiah will rise first, then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds.
We will all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.

Read Matthew 24 carefully on the order. Yahshua says that immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun is darkened, the sign of the Son of Man appears, and then he sends out his messengers with a great sound of a trumpet to gather his chosen ones from the four winds (Matthew 24:29-31). That is the same event Paul describes: the dead raised, the living changed into bodies that do not corrupt, all at the trumpet. It is a resurrection at the last trumpet, not a quiet removal beforehand. The seventh messenger sounds and the announcement is made that the kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Adonai and of his Messiah (Revelation 11:15). That case is built on explicit text and needs nothing else propping it up.

The prophets sound the same alarm on the same day: blow the trumpet in Zion, sound an alarm in my holy mountain (Joel 2:1), and the great trumpet that brings home the ones who were ready to perish (Isaiah 27:13; compare Zephaniah 1:14-16).

blocks.title: Watch, Because You Are Not Told To Calculate
blocks.v: Yahshua said no one knows the day or the hour of his return (Matthew 24:36). Scripture does not tie that statement to this feast in so many words, so treat the connection as a pattern worth weighing rather than a proof. What is not optional is the instruction attached to it. It is not calculation. It is readiness (Matthew 24:42-44; Matthew 25:1-13). Ten virgins all had lamps. Five had oil.

However on the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement. It shall be a holy convocation to you. You shall afflict yourselves … You shall do no kind of work … It shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest to you, and you shall afflict your souls. In the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you shall keep your Sabbath.

The instruction. One day a year the high priest went behind the veil with blood. He bathed, put off his glory and put on plain linen, offered first for himself, then took two goats. Lots were cast: one goat for YHWH, whose blood went into the most holy place, and one goat sent away alive, carrying the iniquities of the people to a solitary land (Leviticus 16:3-22).
The fulfillment. The book of Hebrews is essentially a commentary on this day.

But Messiah having come as a high priest of the coming good things … nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.

He did not enter a copy but heaven itself, to appear before the face of Elohim for us (Hebrews 9:24). He was offered once to bear the sins of many, and will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those who are eagerly waiting (Hebrews 9:28). Where the old priests stood daily offering sacrifices that could never take away sins, he offered one sacrifice forever and sat down (Hebrews 10:11-12). Isaiah saw both goats in one person: wounded for our transgressions, and YHWH laid on him the iniquity of us all (Isaiah 53:5-6).
What is still ahead. Zechariah puts a national day of mourning and recognition at the end.
I will pour on David's house and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of supplication. They will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him.

And the day after that mourning, a fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness (Zechariah 13:1). There is one more thread: the Jubilee trumpet was sounded on the Day of Atonement, and liberty was proclaimed throughout the land, every man returning to his possession and to his family (Leviticus 25:9-10). Debts cleared, land returned, slaves released, all announced on this day. That is the year Yahshua stood up and read out of Isaiah 61 and said it was fulfilled in their hearing (Luke 4:18-19).

blocks.title: Afflict Your Souls
blocks.v: Leviticus commands the affliction and does not define the word in the chapter, so let Scripture define it. I afflicted my soul with fasting (Psalm 35:13), and Isaiah 58:3 and 5 put fasting and afflicting the soul side by side before telling you what YHWH is actually after with it (Isaiah 58:6-7). Ezra proclaimed a fast to afflict themselves before their Elohim (Ezra 8:21). So the fasting is Scripture's own application, not a tradition bolted on. This is the one appointed time that is not a celebration. Humble yourself, search out what you have been carrying, and make it right. Pride is what keeps a man from doing that honestly, and unforgiveness is what pride looks like once it has been sitting a while. If forgiveness is the root of deliverance, then this day is the appointed time for it.

sections.heading: Tabernacles, Sukkot, and the Eighth Day

blocks.v: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the feast of booths for seven days to YHWH. … On the eighth day shall be a holy convocation to you … It is a solemn assembly.

You shall dwell in booths seven days. All who are native born in Israel shall dwell in booths, that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.

The instruction. Leave your house. Build a temporary shelter out of branches and live in it for a week. Take the fruit of majestic trees, palm branches, leafy boughs, and willows of the brook, and rejoice before YHWH seven days (Leviticus 23:40). Deuteronomy 16:13-15 says it twice: you shall rejoice, and you shall be altogether joyful. Nehemiah 8:14-18 records the whole city doing it again after the exile, with very great gladness.
What it pictures. That YHWH dwells with his people, and that this life is the temporary structure, not the permanent one. A week in a booth teaches what a thousand sermons on contentment cannot.
The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

The Hebrew word for the shelter is sukkah, and the command to dwell in them is Leviticus 23:42. When John writes that the Word lived among us, the Greek verb is skenoo, from skene, a tent. He pitched his tent among us. He tabernacled in flesh. And the scene John is given at the end of the book is the feast made permanent.
Behold, Elohim's dwelling is with people; and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and Elohim himself will be with them as their Elohim.

Yahshua taught publicly at this feast, and on the last and greatest day of it he stood and cried out that anyone who is thirsty should come to him and drink, promising rivers of living water, which John explains was the Spirit (John 7:2, 37-39). In the same setting he said he is the light of the world (John 8:12). Water and light, at the feast of dwelling.

The eighth day. Scripture sets the eighth day apart from the seven. It is its own holy convocation, its own solemn assembly, after the booths come down. Seven is the number of the completed cycle. Eight is what comes after the cycle is finished: new creation, new beginning. Leviticus 23 does not tell us what the eighth day pictures, so what follows is offered as an interpretation rather than a commandment. I believe this is where the marriage supper of the Lamb belongs.

Let's rejoice and be exceedingly glad, and let's give the glory to him. For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready. … Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.

And immediately after that wedding John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and the bride coming down adorned for her husband (Revelation 21:1-2). Seven days of dwelling with him, then the eighth day, and everything is made new. Weigh it against the text and hold it loosely where the text is quiet.

blocks.title: This One Is Kept After He Returns
blocks.v: Zechariah 14:16-19 says that everyone left of the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, YHWH of Armies, and to keep the feast of booths, with consequences for the families that refuse. That is after his return, in his Kingdom, with the nations included. Anyone who says these appointed times were done away with has to explain why the nations are keeping this one in the age to come.
One passage gets quoted more than any other to argue that these days no longer matter, so it is worth reading slowly.
Let no one therefore judge you in eating or drinking, or with respect to a feast day or a new moon or a Sabbath day, which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Messiah's.

Paul does not say the feast days are cancelled. He says do not let anyone judge you about how you keep them, and he says they are a shadow of things to come, which is future tense for things still ahead. A shadow is proof that something real is standing there casting it. You do not throw out the shadow because you have found the body. You look at the shadow and it tells you the shape of the one it belongs to. The priesthood serves a copy and shadow of heavenly things (Hebrews 8:5), and the instructions hold a shadow of the good things to come (Hebrews 10:1). Whatever else anyone makes of the passage, Paul never writes that YHWH's Sabbath and appointed times have been abolished.
Scripture keeps the appointed times running long after the resurrection and long into the future:
He says he will not eat the Passover again until it is fulfilled in the Kingdom of Elohim. A future Passover is on his calendar.
The disciples are gathered on the day of Pentecost because they were keeping it.
Paul sails after the days of unleavened bread and hurries to be in Jerusalem for Pentecost.
Paul tells a mostly non-Jewish assembly in Corinth to keep the feast.
Passover and the feast of the seventh month are being kept in the temple Ezekiel is shown.
The nations go up yearly to keep the feast of booths after his return.
From one new moon to another and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh comes to worship before him.

The appointed times are his teaching tool. Amos 3:7 says he does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets. Leviticus 23 is that revelation written as a calendar. Four lamps have already been lit exactly on schedule. Three are still waiting.

If we are going to ask people to test Sunday, Christmas, Easter, and the claim that Torah was abolished, then we have to hold our own teaching to the same standard. Deuteronomy 4:2 and 12:32 forbid adding to his instructions as clearly as they forbid taking away from them, and adding usually happens by accident, through a phrase repeated so often that nobody checks it anymore.
Four questions to run everything through, this handout included:

items: Where does Scripture command it? Chapter and verse, not a teaching you heard.
Where does Torah establish it? The foundation has to carry the weight.
Do the Prophets and Writings confirm it? Two or three witnesses, not one favorite verse.
Do the Apostolic writings agree with that foundation? They never overturn it.

blocks.title: Where This Study Draws The Line
blocks.v: Three things in this handout are labeled as interpretation rather than commandment, on purpose: the eighth day as the place of the marriage supper, the two loaves as the two houses, and the Wednesday timeline of the execution week. Each one is argued from the text, and each one should be weighed rather than swallowed. And where Scripture stops speaking, we stop calling our interpretation a commandment.
None of this is ritual. It is relationship with a schedule attached. Here is how to start, without pretending to be something you are not.

items: Read Leviticus 23 out loud, start to finish, with your family. It takes about ten minutes. Most believers have never heard the whole chapter read in one sitting.
Put the dates on your calendar for the coming year. You cannot keep an appointment you do not know about.
Keep Passover. Read Exodus 12 at the table. Tell your children what the blood means. That telling is commanded (Exodus 12:26-27; Deuteronomy 6:6-7).
Put the leaven out for the week. Let the physical search prompt the spiritual one.
Count the fifty days. Counting makes you pay attention. It is the only feast that requires it.
Rest on Trumpets and listen. Blow a shofar if you have one. Ask yourself honestly whether you would be ready if that trumpet were the one.
Fast and repent on Atonement. Make the list. Forgive the people on it. Ask forgiveness from the people you have wronged. Do not carry it into another year.
Build a booth and rejoice. Get out of the house, get around other believers, and be altogether joyful. It is commanded, and it is good for a family.

blocks.title: Start Where You Are
blocks.v: You do not have to keep all seven perfectly this year to begin. Keep the next one that comes. Learn it, teach it to your household, and let him build on it. Obedience is a walk, not a single step, and he is patient with those who are actually walking.

topics.title: The Day of Trumpets
topics.subtitle: Yom Teruah, the appointed time no man can pin to a date.
topics.note: A Midrash Study on the Day of Trumpets and the Return of Yahshua Scripture quoted from the World English Bible with the sacred names restored. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Yahshua said no one knows the day or the hour of his return. In the same discourse he said that those who watch the tree will know the season, and Paul said the day will not overtake the children of light like a thief. Both are true, and Yom Teruah is where they meet. It is the one appointed time YHWH placed on the first day of a month, the head of the month, and marked with a trumpet blast. A day you cannot pin down, inside a season you cannot miss if you are watching.
Only two passages in the instructions of YHWH command this day. Both are short. Both are loaded.

YHWH spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, shall be a solemn rest to you, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work; and you shall offer an offering made by fire to YHWH.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work. It is a day of blowing of trumpets to you.

Now notice what is not there. There is no explanation. No historical event attached. No Passover lamb, no exodus, no wilderness booths. Every other appointed day in Leviticus 23 comes with a reason written into the text. This one comes with a sound and a silence.
That silence is not an oversight. It is the design of the day.
This is the foundation everything else rests on, so we build it slowly.
The word itself

The Hebrew word is moed, plural moedim. It does not mean holiday, and it does not mean festival in the way we use that word. It means an appointed time, a fixed season, a set meeting. It carries the sense of a rendezvous, a scheduled appearance, a meeting placed on the calendar by someone with the authority to place it there.
Elohim said, Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years.

That word seasons is moedim. On day four of creation, before there was a Hebrew, before there was an Israel, before there was a scroll of instructions, YHWH hung the sun and the moon in the sky and said they exist to mark his appointments.
The appointed times are not Jewish culture. They are written into the sky.
He appointed the moon for seasons. The sun knows when to set.
Whose feasts are they
YHWH spoke to Moses, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, The set feasts of YHWH, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my set feasts.

Read that last line again. My set feasts. He does not call them the feasts of Israel. He does not call them the feasts of the Jews. He signs his own name to them. They belong to YHWH. Israel was simply the household that was handed the calendar to keep.
These are the set feasts of YHWH, even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed season.
In their appointed season. Not whenever it is convenient. Not on a date a council picked centuries later. In the season he set.

blocks.title: A Word About Holy Convocation
blocks.v: The phrase is miqra qodesh. Miqra comes from the root qara, to call, to proclaim, to summon, to read. It means a sacred assembly, a called gathering, a day his people are summoned to. It is worth saying plainly that it does not mean rehearsal. That is a popular teaching and it is not what the word carries. The prophetic weight of these days is real, but it comes from the events Scripture records landing on them, not from a meaning pressed into a Hebrew noun.

blocks.title: Season, Not Date
blocks.v: Here is the key that unlocks the whole study. A moed is a season, and a season has an arrival you can feel before you can pinpoint it. You do not need a calendar to know autumn is coming. The air changes. The light changes. The leaves turn. You know the season long before you could name the exact hour it began. That is the entire prophetic logic of this day.

Yom Teruah means the Day of Blowing, or more literally the Day of Shouting. The Hebrew teruah is a specific kind of sound. Not a smooth note. A broken, urgent, staccato blast. An alarm. A war cry. A shout.
Scripture uses teruah for several things, and every one of them preaches.
Teruah as alarm and assembly
In Numbers 10:1-10 YHWH commands two silver trumpets. Read carefully what they are for:

items: A long blast gathers the whole congregation to the door of the tent. Numbers 10:3
A teruah, the broken alarm blast, breaks the camp and moves it out. Numbers 10:5-6
A teruah in war means you will be remembered before YHWH your Elohim, and you will be saved from your enemies. Numbers 10:9
And trumpets are blown in the day of your gladness, in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months. Numbers 10:10

blocks.v: Assembly. Movement. Remembrance. Deliverance. That is the vocabulary of the trumpet, and it is the vocabulary of the return of Yahshua.
Teruah as the sound that brings walls down
When they make a long blast with the ram's horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down flat.
The trumpet and the shout together bring down what looked permanent (Joshua 6:20).
Teruah as the sound of joy

items: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim shouted for joy. Job 38:7
At the laying of the foundation, the shout of joy and the weeping of the old men mixed together until no one could tell the two apart. Ezra 3:11-13

blocks.v: Joy and grief in the same sound. That is what a trumpet does to a heart that has been waiting a very long time.
Teruah as the sound of the King arriving
Elohim has gone up with a shout, YHWH with the sound of a trumpet.
Blessed are the people who know the joyful sound. They walk, YHWH, in the light of your face.
That phrase, the joyful sound, is teruah. Blessed are the people who know the sound. Not the people who know the date. The people who recognize the sound when they hear it.

sections.heading: Why It Is Called the Day No One Knows

blocks.v: What the text actually establishes

Every appointed time in Leviticus 23 is anchored to a numbered day of a month. Passover is the fourteenth. Unleavened Bread runs the fifteenth through the twenty first. Yom Kippur is the tenth. Sukkot is the fifteenth.
Yom Teruah is the only moed that falls on the first day of a month. Every other one is counted from a date already fixed inside a month that is already running. This one begins when the month begins.

And in Scripture the month is tied to the moon. The Hebrew word for month is chodesh, from the root chadash, to be new, to renew. Psalm 104:19 says he appointed the moon for the moedim, and the trumpets were sounded at the beginnings of the months (Numbers 10:10; Numbers 28:11). The moon marks the months. That much is plain.
Now the honest part, in three places

First, the mechanism. It is commonly taught, and this handout used to teach it, that the month cannot be declared until witnesses confirm a first visible crescent. There is no such commandment in Torah. No verse instructs anyone to go out, look for a sliver, and declare the month on the testimony of two men. Scripture ties the month to the moon and stops. Where it stops speaking, we stop calling our interpretation a commandment (Deuteronomy 4:2; 12:32).
Blow the trumpet at the New Moon, at the full moon, on our feast day.

Second, this verse. It is often said that the Hebrew behind New Moon here carries the sense of concealment. It does not. That word is chodesh, from chadash, to renew. The concealment argument attaches to the second word in the verse, keseh, and keseh is the word most translations render as full moon. Its meaning is genuinely disputed. A verse that scholars cannot agree on is not a foundation. This handout no longer builds the hiddenness of the day on Psalm 81:3.

Third, 1 Samuel 20. This chapter gets claimed by both sides, and both sides have something in it. David says tomorrow is the new moon and Jonathan says it back to him (1 Samuel 20:5, 18), which shows they knew the day before it arrived. The observance also runs across two days (20:27), which shows some flexibility in how it was kept. Read the chapter and let it say what it says. It does not settle the calendar question, and we should not pretend it settles it for us.

blocks.title: What Survives, And It Is Enough
blocks.v: Strip out everything Torah does not command and this is what is left standing, which is the part that mattered all along: Yom Teruah is the only appointed time YHWH placed on the head of a month rather than inside one. Yahshua said the day and hour of his return is known to the Father alone (Matthew 24:36), and he said he returns at a trumpet, after the tribulation, to gather his own (Matthew 24:29-31). Those are his words, not a tradition, and the case does not need a mechanism propped under it.
And the tradition we do not need

You will hear it taught that no man knows the day or hour was a common Jewish idiom for this feast, and that everyone in the first century would have heard Yahshua say it and immediately thought of Yom Teruah.

Be straight with people about this. That specific idiom claim is not written in Scripture. It comes from later rabbinic and traditional sources. We do not build doctrine on rabbinic tradition, and we should not build it on our own favorite explanations either.

blocks.title: Hold It At The Right Weight
blocks.v: Scripture does not explicitly tie Matthew 24:36 to this feast. Treat the connection as a pattern worth weighing rather than a proof, and let the explicit passages carry the argument. That is not a retreat. It is the difference between a teaching that holds up under examination and one that collapses the first time somebody asks for chapter and verse.
The statement
But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
But of that day or that hour no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father. Watch, keep alert, and pray; for you do not know when the time is.
The parable that names the feast without naming it
Look at every element of Matthew 25:1-13, the ten virgins:

items: A bridegroom whose arrival time is not announced.
Ten who are waiting, all of whom believe they are ready.
Lamps and oil, the difference between profession and preparation.
A delay long enough that all ten fall asleep.
A cry at midnight, a shout in the dark, waking everyone at once.
A door that shuts.
And the closing line: watch therefore, for you do not know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming. Matthew 25:13

blocks.v: A shout in the darkness that wakes the sleeping and separates the ready from the unready. That is a teruah.
The verse that changes everything
Right before Yahshua says no one knows the day, he says this:

Now from the fig tree learn this parable: When its branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near. Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.

See the fig tree and all the trees. When they are already budding, you see it and know by your own selves that the summer is already near. Even so you also, when you see these things happening, know that the Kingdom of Elohim is near.

blocks.title: The Whole Teaching In One Line
blocks.v: You will not know the day. You will know the season. He did not offer that as a suggestion. He said you know. He expects it. A man who watches the tree knows summer is coming, and he still cannot tell you the hour summer started.
Failing to know the season is a rebuke

When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, A shower is coming, and so it happens. When a south wind blows, you say, There will be a scorching heat, and it happens. You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you do not interpret this time?

items: You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you cannot discern the signs of the times. Matthew 16:2-3
Because you did not know the time of your visitation. Luke 19:44

blocks.v: Jerusalem missed him. Not because the information was hidden, but because they were not watching the season. That warning lands on us too.
The clearest passage in Scripture on this

But concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need that anything be written to you. For you yourselves know well that the day of YHWH comes like a thief in the night... But you, brothers, are not in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief. You are all children of light and children of the day. We do not belong to the night, nor to darkness, so then let us not sleep, as the rest do, but let us watch and be sober.

Sit with this one. Paul says the day comes like a thief, and then immediately says it will not come like a thief to you. Why? Because you are not in darkness. Because you are watching. Because you know the times and the seasons.

The Greek word there is kairos, appointed season, the same idea used to render moed in the Greek Scriptures. The children of light know the moedim. That is the difference between being caught and being ready.
If therefore you will not watch, I will come as a thief, and you will not know what hour I will come on you.
Read the condition. If you will not watch. The thief language is conditional, and the condition is watchfulness (see also Revelation 16:15).
Holding the tension honestly
It is not for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.

Someone will bring this verse to you. Handle it plainly. The disciples were asking for a restoration schedule so they could sit down and calculate. Yahshua refused to feed date setting. He did not cancel watchfulness, because Matthew 24, Matthew 25, Mark 13, and 1 Thessalonians 5 all command it.

blocks.title: Draw The Line Here
blocks.v: Date setting is forbidden. Season watching is commanded. Those are not the same activity, and confusing them has wrecked a lot of faith.
This is where Yom Teruah stops being a nice pattern and becomes the literal mechanism of our hope.

Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.

For the Master himself will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of Elohim. The dead in Messiah will rise first, then we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Master in the air.
Look at the components: a shout, a voice, a trumpet. That is a teruah with a resurrection attached to it.

But immediately after the oppression of those days... he will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.

Note the timing marker Yahshua placed himself. After the oppression of those days. The gathering happens at the trumpet, after the tribulation, not before it. This is the resurrection of the dead and the changing of the living into glorified bodies.
The seventh angel sounded, and great voices in heaven followed, saying, The kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Master, and of his Messiah. He will reign forever and ever!
The last trumpet. The seventh. The kingdom transfers at a trumpet blast.
The prophets said it first

It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and those who were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and they will worship YHWH in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.

Do not read past that one. The great trumpet gathers the ones scattered into Assyria. That is the northern house, the tribes who were exiled and lost their identity. The trumpet is the sound that brings the outcasts home and puts the two sticks back into one hand (Ezekiel 37:15-22).
The Master YHWH will blow the trumpet, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.
Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain, for the day of YHWH comes, for it is close at hand.
Blow the trumpet in Zion. Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly.
The great day of YHWH is near. A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fortified cities.
Does the trumpet alarm sound in a city without the people being afraid?
Blow the horn in Gibeah, and the trumpet in Ramah.
At Sinai the voice of the trumpet sounded loud and long, and grew louder and louder.
Every prophet who describes the Day of YHWH reaches for the same instrument.
Leviticus 23:24 calls it a zikhron teruah, a memorial of blowing. Memorial means remembrance, and remembrance runs in both directions.
Then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then you will be remembered before YHWH your Elohim, and you will be saved from your enemies.
The trumpet is the sound of being remembered by YHWH.

Then those who feared YHWH spoke one with another; and YHWH listened and heard, and a book of memory was written before him for those who feared YHWH and who honored his name... They shall be mine, says YHWH of Armies, my own possession in the day that I make.
There is a book with names in it, and there is a day when it is opened (Daniel 7:10; Revelation 20:12). The trumpet is the sound that announces the day has come.
Here is the argument that closes the case for anyone paying attention.
The spring feasts were fulfilled to the day
Yahshua died as the lamb, at Passover. For indeed Messiah, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place. 1 Corinthians 5:7
His body in the tomb, without corruption, without leaven. Acts 2:27
He rose as the firstfruits of those who are asleep. 1 Corinthians 15:20-23
The Spirit poured out when the day had fully come. Acts 2:1
Four appointments. Four fulfillments. Not one of them was approximate. Every single one landed on the exact appointed day.
So what does that tell you about the fall feasts
Three remain: Trumpets, Atonement, and Tabernacles. If he kept the first four appointments to the hour, he is not going to improvise the last three.
Let no one therefore judge you in eating or drinking, or with respect to a feast day or a new moon or a Sabbath day, which are a shadow of the things to come; but the body is Messiah's.

Read it carefully, because this verse gets used backwards constantly. Paul does not say the appointed times are cancelled. He says do not let people judge you for keeping them, and then he says they are a shadow of things to come. Future tense, written decades after the resurrection. The shadow is still pointing at something. Whatever else anyone makes of the passage, Paul never writes that YHWH's Sabbath and appointed times have been abolished.

sections.heading: Why Followers of Yahshua Should Keep This Day

blocks.v: Here is the case, laid out plainly, without arguing with anybody.
1. He called them his.
These are my set feasts (Leviticus 23:2). Not Jewish feasts. His. If they belong to him, and we belong to him, the question mostly answers itself.
2. They were never given only to one bloodline.

items: One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you. Exodus 12:49
One statute for you and for the foreigner, forever throughout your generations. Numbers 15:15-16
Let no foreigner who has joined himself to YHWH say, YHWH will surely separate me from his people. Them I will bring to my holy mountain. Isaiah 56:3, 6-7

blocks.v: 3. You have already been brought near.

You were at that time separate from Messiah, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise... But now in Messiah Yahshua you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Messiah... So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and of the household of Elohim.
You were grafted into the olive tree (Romans 11:17-24). The tree did not become yours. You became part of it. A grafted branch does not get a different calendar than the tree.
4. The first followers kept them.

items: They were gathered together on Shavuot when the Spirit fell. Acts 2:1
Paul arranged his travel around keeping the appointed times. Acts 18:21; Acts 20:16
Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old yeast, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. 1 Corinthians 5:8

blocks.v: That last one was written to a mostly non-Jewish congregation in Greece. Let us keep the feast.
5. Yahshua kept them, and we follow him.

items: He went up to the Feast of Tabernacles. John 7:2, 10 I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer. Luke 22:15
He who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked. 1 John 2:6 If you love me, keep my commandments. John 14:15
Do not think that I came to destroy the Torah or the prophets. I did not come to destroy, but to fulfill. Matthew 5:17-19

blocks.v: 6. They are still being kept in the age to come.

items: Everyone who is left of all the nations will go up from year to year to worship the King and to keep the feast of booths. Zechariah 14:16-19
From one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me. Isaiah 66:22-23
The appointed times observed in the restored kingdom. Ezekiel 45:21-25

blocks.v: If the nations keep them in the kingdom, there is no version of this where they were abolished in between.
7. And the practical one.
You cannot watch a clock you refuse to look at. He said watch. He tied his return to a trumpet. He put a trumpet on the calendar. Keeping this day is how you stay oriented to the season.
Now the guardrail, because this is where people get hurt. Keeping a feast does not save anybody. It never did.
Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me. New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I cannot stand evil assemblies. My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts.

Stop and feel that. He is not condemning the days he himself commanded. He is condemning days kept by hands full of blood and hearts full of pride. Read the next verses. He tells them to wash, to cease from evil, to relieve the oppressed, to plead for the widow.
I hate, I despise your feasts... But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream. Amos 5:21-24

items: These people draw near to me with their mouth, and honor me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. Matthew 15:8-9
What does YHWH require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your Elohim? Micah 6:8

blocks.title: Say It Plainly
blocks.v: Do not blow a shofar and then go back to holding a grudge. Do not put on tzitzit and refuse to forgive your brother. Do not learn a Hebrew word and stay proud. That is exactly what he said he hates. The day is an appointment with a Person. Keep the appointment, but bring your heart.
This is the thread we never want to miss, because it is the reason this ministry exists. The trumpet in Scripture is not only a warning. It is the sound of release.

Then you shall sound the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land. You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee to you; and each of you shall return to his own property, and each of you shall return to his family.
Debts cancelled. Slaves released. Property restored. Families reunited. All of it announced by a horn.
And when Yahshua stood up in the synagogue to announce his own ministry, this is the passage he reached for:

The Spirit of the Master YHWH is on me, because YHWH has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound... to proclaim the year of YHWH's favor.
The trumpet season is jubilee season. Release season. And Yahshua tied our own release directly to whether we release others.

items: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. Matthew 6:14-15
The servant forgiven an unpayable debt who would not release a small one, and was handed over to the tormentors. Matthew 18:21-35
Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone. Mark 11:25

blocks.title: The Order Of Things
blocks.v: Unforgiveness is a debt you are still choosing to collect on after the trumpet has announced that the debts are cancelled. It is standing in the middle of jubilee with somebody's account still open. And underneath unforgiveness, every single time, is pride. Pride says I am owed. Pride says what they did is bigger than what I was forgiven. Humility is what lets the hand open.

That is why the trumpet comes before atonement on the calendar. The alarm sounds, and then there are days to go get your heart right. If you want a real Yom Teruah, do not just hear a horn. Go release somebody.
There is one more role the trumpet belongs to, and it is not the King's. It is ours.

If, when he sees the sword come on the land, he blows the trumpet and warns the people, then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not heed the warning, if the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head... But if the watchman sees the sword come and does not blow the trumpet, and the people are not warned... I will require his blood at the watchman's hand.

items: Cry aloud. Do not spare. Lift up your voice like a trumpet. Isaiah 58:1 I will stand at my watch, and set myself on the ramparts, and will look out to see what he will say to me. Habakkuk 2:1
Watch therefore, for you do not know when the lord of the house is coming, lest coming suddenly he might find you sleeping. What I tell you, I tell all: Watch. Mark 13:34-37

blocks.v: The watchman does not know the hour either. That was never his job. His job is to be awake and to have his lips on the horn.

sections.heading: The Day They Read the Book

blocks.v: One passage almost nobody connects to this feast, and it is one of the most beautiful in Scripture.
All the people gathered themselves together as one man into the wide place... and they spoke to Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the Torah of Moses... on the first day of the seventh month.
That is Yom Teruah. They read from morning until midday. And when the people heard the instructions of YHWH after generations of exile, they wept. They realized how far they had drifted.
Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for this day is holy to our Master. Do not be grieved, for the joy of YHWH is your strength.

That is what this day looks like when it is done right. The scattered people gather. The book is opened. Hearts break over what was lost. And then joy, feasting, and portions sent to whoever has nothing prepared.
Grieve over what was lost, then eat, then go feed somebody who has nothing. That is Yom Teruah.
Straight from the text, with nothing added.

1. A holy convocation. Gather. Do not do this alone if you can help it. Leviticus 23:24; Hebrews 10:25 2. A solemn rest. No regular work. Lay the job down. Leviticus 23:24-25; Numbers 29:1 3. Blow the trumpet. A shofar if you have one, whatever horn you have if you do not. Make the sound.
Leviticus 23:24; Numbers 10:10; Psalm 81:3
4. Read the book out loud. Follow the Nehemiah 8 pattern. Leviticus 23, Numbers 10, Matthew 24 and 25, 1
Thessalonians 4 and 5, 1 Corinthians 15.
5. Search your heart and release your debts. Forgive before Atonement comes. Matthew 6:14-15; Leviticus
6. Eat well, and send a portion to someone who has nothing prepared. Nehemiah 8:10
What is tradition, and what is Scripture

Be honest with people about this. The name Rosh Hashanah, the ten Days of Awe, apples and honey, the specific shofar sequences, the books of life and death ceremony, and the wedding customs sometimes taught alongside this day are all tradition. Some of it is beautiful. None of it is commanded.

The same honesty has to cut toward our own side of the aisle. A required crescent sighting is not commanded either, and neither is a calculated conjunction. Torah ties the month to the moon and leaves the method unwritten. Anyone who tells you their reckoning is the commanded one should be asked for the verse.

What is commanded is short: rest, gather, blow, and remember. Do not add a burden Scripture did not put there, and do not despise a brother who keeps a custom you do not. If one man marks the day by a sighted moon and another marks it by calculation, do not break fellowship over a sliver of light.
One man esteems one day as more important. Another esteems every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind. He who observes the day, observes it to the Master.
The point was never precision. The point is that you are watching.
The whole study in one place:

items: YHWH set appointments in the sky on day four of creation, before there was a single Hebrew on the earth.
He called them his feasts, and commanded that they be kept in their appointed season.
He put exactly one of them on the first day of a month, the head of the month, and made it a day of shouting. The only moed that is not counted from a date already fixed.
Torah ties the month to the moon and does not hand us the mechanism, so we hold our reckoning with an open hand and do not call it a commandment.
He fulfilled the first four appointments in Yahshua, precisely, on the day.
Yahshua said he returns at a trumpet, after the tribulation, to gather his own and raise the dead.
He said no one knows the day or the hour.
And he said, in the same breath, that those who watch the tree will know the season, and that the day will not overtake the children of light like a thief.

blocks.v: So we do not set dates. We stay awake. We keep the appointment. We keep our lamps full. We keep our accounts released and our hands open. And when that broken, urgent, joyful sound goes up, we are not startled.

blocks.title: The Last Word
blocks.v: We are the people who know the joyful sound (Psalm 89:15). Blow the horn. Open the book. Forgive somebody. He is coming back at a trumpet, and he has never once missed an appointment.
