Two sources to avoid

items: Commercial tissue vendor blogs. The claims are mostly accurate but they sell porcine tissue for a living, and citing them hands a critic an easy dismissal.
The MYH4 muscle gene study. It gets passed around as proof of similarity. It actually documents a difference: humans do not express that gene and pigs do. Citing it hands the argument away.

topics.title: The Tithe
topics.subtitle: What Scripture Actually Says
topics.note: A Midrash Study from Abraham to Yahshua Scripture quoted from the World English Bible, divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Few subjects stir up more guilt, more arguments, and more confusion than the tithe. Some were told that anything less than ten percent of their paycheck to the church is robbing Elohim. Others were told the tithe is dead and giving is optional. This study sets both of those aside and asks one question: what does the text actually say? What was the tithe made of, who received it, what was it for, and how do we walk in the heart of it today without calling our own interpretation a commandment?
Most people were taught that tithing began with Abraham. So we start by reading exactly what Abraham did.

Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of Elohim Most High. He blessed him, and said, "Blessed be Abram of Elohim Most High, possessor of heaven and earth. Blessed be Elohim Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand." Abram gave him a tenth of all.

Hebrews 7:4 tells us what that tenth came from: the spoils of the battle Abram had just won when he rescued Lot. It was not his wages, and nothing in the text says it was a yearly practice. It is one tenth, given one time, to one priest.

Then read the next few verses, which are rarely preached. Abram told the king of Sodom he would not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap, so that no one could say a man made Abram rich. He kept none of the remainder for himself. Only what his young men had eaten and the share of the allies who fought with him was set aside (Genesis
Jacob's Vow
At Bethel, Jacob made a conditional vow. If Elohim would be with him, keep him on the journey, give him bread to eat and clothing to wear, and bring him back to his father's house in peace, then:
Of all that you will give me I will surely give a tenth to you.
That is a promise Jacob made, with conditions attached, not an instruction YHWH gave him.

blocks.title: What We Learn
blocks.v: Before Torah we see one tenth from war spoils and one personal vow. Both show a heart that honors YHWH as the source of everything. Neither one is a standing command, and neither one is a weekly percentage of wages. For the command, we have to go to Torah.
All the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the trees, is YHWH's. It is holy to YHWH.
Verse 32 adds every tenth animal of the herd and the flock, whatever passes under the rod. Look at what is on the list: crops and animals. The tithe was the increase of the land YHWH gave Israel.
The tithe of seed, fruit, herd, and flock is holy to YHWH. It may be redeemed with money by adding a fifth to its value.
The tithe is given to the Levites as their inheritance in return for their service at the Tent of Meeting, because they have no land inheritance in Israel.
The Levites give a tenth of the tithe they receive, the best of it, to the priests.
Deuteronomy 12:5-7,
The tithe is brought to the place YHWH chooses and eaten there before Him with rejoicing, with
17-18 the Levite included.
The tithe of grain, new wine, and oil is eaten before YHWH at the place He chooses. If the distance is too great, it may be turned into money and spent there on food and drink for rejoicing.
Every third year the tithe is stored in the towns for the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
In the third year, the year of tithing, the giver declares before YHWH that he has given it as commanded.
The Tithe That Surprises People

You shall surely tithe all the increase of your seed, that which comes out of the field year by year. You shall eat before YHWH your Elohim, in the place which he shall choose to cause his name to dwell, the tithe of your grain, of your new wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock; that you may learn to fear YHWH your Elohim always.

If the journey was too long to carry it, Israel could sell the tithe, carry the money, and then spend it at the feast on whatever they desired: cattle, sheep, wine, or strong drink. Then they were to eat before YHWH and rejoice with their household, and not forsake the Levite (Deuteronomy 14:24-27). Part of the tithe paid for celebrating before
YHWH. The stated purpose was that they would learn to fear Him always.
The Third Year Tithe

At the end of every three years you shall bring all the tithe of your increase in the same year, and shall store it within your gates. The Levite, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, as well as the foreigner living among you, the fatherless, and the widow who are within your gates shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied; that YHWH your Elohim may bless you in all the work of your hand which you do.
Where Money Shows Up

In the tithe instructions, money appears in only two places: to carry the tithe to the feast when the distance is too far (Deuteronomy 14:24-25), and to redeem it by paying its value plus a fifth (Leviticus 27:31). In both cases the tithe itself is still produce and animals.
Tithe and Firstfruits Are Not the Same

The firstfruits were a separate offering: the first of the harvest, brought in a basket to the priest with a spoken confession of what YHWH had done (Exodus 23:19; Deuteronomy 26:1-11). The tithe was a tenth of the increase. Scripture keeps them distinct, and so should we.

blocks.title: Where Scripture Stops
blocks.v: Jewish tradition counts these as separate tithes: one for the Levites, a second eaten at the feasts, and a third year tithe for the poor. Others read them as one tithe used in different ways. The text does not settle the count for us, so we will not build a rule on it. What the text does settle is the purpose. The tithe fed those who served YHWH, paid for rejoicing before Him, and fed the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.

Will a man rob Elohim? Yet you rob me! But you say, "How have we robbed you?" In tithes and offerings. You are cursed with the curse; for you rob me, even this whole nation. Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house, and test me now in this, says YHWH of Armies, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there will not be room enough for.
Malachi prophesied after Judah returned from exile and the temple was rebuilt, around the same period as Nehemiah. Nehemiah lets us see what the storehouse was and what had gone wrong.

items: The people covenanted to bring the tithes of their ground to the Levites, and the Levites were to bring a tenth of those tithes up to the storerooms of the house of Elohim. Nehemiah 10:37-39
Nehemiah found the Levites had not been given their portions, so the Levites and singers had fled back to their own fields to survive. Nehemiah 13:10
He set it right, and all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, new wine, and oil into the treasuries. Nehemiah

blocks.v: The storehouse was rooms in the temple stocked with food for the Levites and priests who served there. Malachi says so himself: that there may be food in my house.

Notice also who YHWH says He will judge just two verses earlier: those who oppress the hired worker in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless, and those who turn away the foreigner (Malachi 3:5). Those are the very people the tithe was meant to feed.

blocks.title: Two Common Misreadings
blocks.v: The storehouse is the church building. The text never says this. The storehouse in Malachi and Nehemiah is temple storerooms holding produce for the Levites. Malachi only rebuked the priests. This one is popular on the other side of the debate, and it does not hold either. Malachi 3:9 says the whole nation was robbing Him. The people held back the tithe, the Levites went hungry, and the service of YHWH's house broke down.

Yahshua rebuked the scribes and Pharisees for tithing mint, dill, and cumin while leaving undone the weightier matters: justice, mercy, and faith. Then He said they ought to have done those weightier things without leaving the tithe undone (Matthew 23:23; Luke 11:42).
He did not throw the tithe out. He put it in its place, underneath justice, mercy, and faith. Any teaching that says Yahshua abolished the tithe has to explain this verse, and it cannot.
The Tither Who Went Home Unjustified
I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.

Those are the words of the Pharisee in Yahshua's parable, standing beside a tax collector who could only beat his chest and ask for mercy. Yahshua said the tax collector went home justified rather than the tither (Luke 18:9-14). A perfect tithe with a proud heart is not righteousness. Pride can hide inside giving just as easily as it hides inside withholding.
The apostolic writings say a great deal about giving. Here is what they actually teach.
Let him who is taught in the word share all good things with him who teaches.
Paul ties it back to the altar: those who serve at the altar share in it, and those who proclaim the good news should live from it.
Elders who labor in the word are worthy of double honor. Paul quotes Deuteronomy 25:4, do not muzzle the ox while it treads the grain.
The Philippians supported Paul's work more than once, and he calls their gift a sweet smelling sacrifice, well pleasing to Elohim.
A collection set aside for the saints in Jerusalem during hardship. It was relief for believers in need, not a tithe.
No one among them lacked, because distribution was made to each according to need.
Paul reminds the elders of Yahshua's words, that it is more blessed to give than to receive.
Pure religion is to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for Elohim loves a cheerful giver.

blocks.title: Where Scripture Stops
blocks.v: No verse in the apostolic writings sets a percentage for believers, and none names a local congregation as the storehouse. If we preach a rule the text does not give, we are calling an interpretation a commandment.
What the text does give is plain: support those who teach you, care for the fatherless and the widow, meet the needs of the saints, and give from a willing heart, not under pressure.

sections.heading: How Our Family Walks It Out

blocks.v: Today there is no temple standing and no Levites serving at an altar to receive the tithe. So we asked what the heart of the tithe is that we can still walk in, and we let Torah answer. In our home we set aside our first ten percent before anything else, and it goes to four places:
Keeping the feasts
Part of the tithe was eaten before YHWH with rejoicing. Deuteronomy 14:23-26
Homeless care bags
The third year tithe fed the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. Deuteronomy 14:28-29; Matthew 25:35-40
Blessing someone in
He who has pity on the poor lends to YHWH; he will reward him. Proverbs 19:17; 1 John 3:17 need
Supporting ministries
Those who teach the word are to share in the good things of those they teach. Galatians 6:6; 1 Corinthians 9:14

We share this as how we apply the pattern, not as a rule for anyone else. Torah names produce and animals, and we have chosen to follow its purposes with what YHWH gives us now. Where Scripture stops speaking, we stop too.

It does not mean stop giving. Yahshua told the Pharisees not to leave the tithe undone, and the apostles taught generous, cheerful giving everywhere they went. It is not an attack on pastors or teachers. Scripture says those who labor in the word are worthy of support. The question is honesty about what the text says, not whether to support them. It does not throw out YHWH's instructions. We are asking what the tithe actually was so we can honor its purpose, not looking for a way out of it.
It does not give anyone permission to judge someone else's giving. Each one gives as he has determined in his heart. That is between them and YHWH.

items: Nobody should be pressured, threatened with a curse, or shamed into giving. Compulsion is the one thing Paul says giving must never be.

blocks.v: Practical, testable, and small enough to actually do.
Read Deuteronomy 14:22-29 as a family. Talk about what the tithe was made of, who it fed, and why YHWH wanted
His people rejoicing before Him.
Check your heart before your budget. Ask YHWH whether you give grudgingly, out of fear, or to be seen. Repent of
any pride hiding in your giving or your withholding.
Set aside first, not last. Decide on what you will set apart and put it aside before anything else is spent, so giving is not
made from leftovers.
Plan for the next feast. Put something aside now so your household can rejoice before YHWH when the appointed time
comes.
Feed someone this week. The fatherless, the widow, the stranger, the man on the corner. Do it quietly.
Support someone who teaches you. Send a gift, meet a need, or write an honest word of thanks to someone who has fed
you the word.
Forgive anyone who used giving against you. If you were shamed, pressured, or cursed over money, release it to
YHWH out loud. Bitterness over it is ground the enemy should not have.
Before Torah: Genesis 14:17-24; Genesis 28:20-22; Hebrews 7:1-10 The tithe in Torah: Leviticus 27:30-33; Numbers 18:21-32; Deuteronomy 12:5-7, 17-19; Deuteronomy 14:22-29; Deuteronomy

Firstfruits: Exodus 23:19; Deuteronomy 26:1-11 Return and the storehouse: 2 Chronicles 31:4-12; Nehemiah 10:35-39; Nehemiah 12:44; Nehemiah 13:10-13; Malachi 3:5-12 Yahshua on the tithe: Matthew 23:23; Luke 11:42; Luke 18:9-14 Supporting those who teach: Deuteronomy 25:4; 1 Corinthians 9:7-14; Galatians 6:6; Philippians 4:15-18; 1 Timothy 5:17-18 Care for the poor: Deuteronomy 15:7-11; Proverbs 19:17; Matthew 25:35-40; Acts 4:32-35; James 1:27; 1 John 3:17-18 The heart of giving: Proverbs 3:9-10; Matthew 6:1-4; Mark 12:41-44; Acts 20:35; 2 Corinthians 8:1-15; 2 Corinthians 9:6-8

topics.title: The Armor of Elohim
topics.subtitle: Putting On What YHWH Wore First
topics.note: A Teaching Study on Ephesians 6:10-18 Scripture quoted from the World English Bible (WEB), divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Most teaching on the armor starts with a Roman soldier. Paul started somewhere older. Nearly every piece he names first appears in the Tanakh, worn by YHWH Himself or by His Messiah. The armor of Elohim is His own armor. When we put it on, we are not assembling religious equipment. We are putting on Yahshua.

blocks.title: How This Study Works
blocks.v: Each piece is taught in four movements: Where Paul got it in the Tanakh, the soldier Paul saw, the word behind it in Hebrew or Greek, and walking it out. Each piece closes with questions for reflection or group discussion.

Finally, be strong in Adonai, and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of Elohim, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against the principalities, against the powers, against the world's rulers of the darkness of this age, and against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places. Therefore, put on the whole armor of Elohim, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and, having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having the utility belt of truth buckled around your waist, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, and having fitted your feet with the preparation of the Good News of peace; above all, taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of Elohim; with all prayer and requests, praying at all times in the Spirit, and being watchful to this end in all perseverance and requests for all the saints.

Before Paul names a single piece, he gives the posture. Stand against the wiles of the devil (v. 11). Withstand in the evil day, and having done all, stand (v. 13). Stand therefore (v. 14). Four times in four verses. The command is not to charge. It is to hold ground that has already been won.
The word Paul uses for wrestling is pale, a word for hand to hand grappling. This is not a battle fought from a distance. It is close, personal, and daily.

And Paul names the enemy clearly: not flesh and blood. The spouse who hurt you, the parent who failed you, the coworker who lied about you. None of them is the real enemy. That changes how a believer fights.

blocks.title: People Are Not The Enemy
blocks.v: When you treat a person as the enemy, you swing at the wrong target and leave the real one untouched. Forgive the person. Resist the enemy. Be subject to Elohim, resist the devil, and he will flee from you (James 4:7).

Notice who is writing. Paul called himself an ambassador in chains (Ephesians 6:20). Rome is the traditional setting for this letter, and in Rome he lived under guard with a soldier assigned to him (Acts 28:16). The gear he describes may have been sitting right in front of him.

Paul was a student of the Scriptures before he was a student of Rome. Line up the pieces with the Tanakh and a pattern appears: the armor belongs to YHWH and His Messiah before it is ever handed to us.
Belt of truth
Isaiah 11:5. The Branch from the root of Jesse wears righteousness and faithfulness as the belt of his waist. Exodus 12:11. Israel eats the Passover with belts fastened, ready to leave.
Breastplate
Isaiah 59:17. YHWH puts on righteousness as a breastplate when He comes to rescue His people.
Shoes of peace
Isaiah 52:7. The beautiful feet of the messenger who publishes peace and announces that Elohim reigns.
Shield of faith
Genesis 15:1. I am your shield. Psalm 91:4. His faithfulness is your shield. Proverbs 30:5. He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
Helmet of salvation
Isaiah 59:17. The helmet of salvation on His head.
Sword of the Spirit
Isaiah 49:2. The Servant's mouth made like a sharp sword. Isaiah 11:4. The Branch strikes with the rod of His mouth. Hosea 6:5. The words of His mouth.
Prayer and watching
Exodus 17:8-13. Moses' raised hands on the hill while Joshua fights in the valley. Isaiah 62:6. Watchmen on the walls, never silent.

Paul uses the same language in Romans: put on the armor of light, and put on Adonai Yahshua Messiah (Romans 13:12, 14). The armor is not a set of techniques. It is Yahshua Himself, worn by His people. That is why walking in the light and wearing the armor turn out to be the same thing.
Stand therefore, having the utility belt of truth buckled around your waist,
Where Paul Got It
Paul did not invent this belt. Isaiah saw it first, worn by the Messiah, the Branch from the root of Jesse.
Righteousness will be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.
Before it was ever our armor, it was His. When you buckle on truth, you are wearing what Yahshua wears.

The belt reaches back even further. On the night of the first Passover, Israel ate with their belts on, sandals on their feet, and staff in hand, ready to walk out of Egypt the moment YHWH said go (Exodus 12:11). Elijah tucked up his garment and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot (1 Kings 18:46). Peter carries the same picture over to the mind (1 Peter
1:13). In Scripture, a fastened belt means ready to move.
The Soldier Paul Saw

The Roman military belt marked a man as a soldier on duty. Men of that world wore long tunics, and before running or fighting they tucked the loose cloth up into the belt so nothing tangled their legs. A loose belt meant a man who was not ready.
The Word Behind It

The Hebrew word for truth is emet. It comes from the root aman, which carries the idea of being firm, steady, and reliable. Emunah, the word for faithfulness in Isaiah 11:5, comes from the same root, and so does the word amen. In Scripture, truth is not only a correct statement. It is something you can put your full weight on.
Paul's Greek word is aletheia. Yahshua used it of Himself: I am the way, the truth, and the life (John 14:6). He used it of the Father's word: Your word is truth (John 17:17).
Walking It Out

Every other piece hangs from the belt. If truth is loose, everything else starts to slide. The enemy rarely brings a new lie. He repeats old ones until they feel true: you are too far gone, you can never forgive that, that is just who you are. Those lies tangle a believer's legs so he cannot move forward.
Truth is not how you feel about yourself today. It is what YHWH has already said. You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free (John 8:32). Freedom starts at the belt.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: Deception is the enemy's first attack because truth is the first piece. His opening move in the garden was a question about what Elohim had said (Genesis 3:1). He still starts there.
For Reflection

items: What lie about yourself have you repeated so long that it feels true?
Which verse answers that lie directly?
Where in your life are you not ready to move if YHWH says go?

blocks.v: and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
Where Paul Got It

Isaiah 59 describes a nation where truth had fallen in the street and justice was nowhere to be found. YHWH saw there was no one to intercede, so His own arm brought salvation. Then Isaiah shows how He dressed for the rescue.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation on his head; and he put on garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a mantle.

A few verses later, the Redeemer comes to Zion for those who turn from their transgression (Isaiah 59:20). The breastplate Paul tells us to put on is the one YHWH wore when He came to rescue a people who could not rescue themselves. We are not building our own righteousness. We are putting on His.
The Soldier Paul Saw

Roman soldiers in Paul's day wore iron body armor. Mail shirts made of thousands of linked rings were common, and some soldiers wore armor made of overlapping iron bands. Either way, it covered the chest and back, where a single blow could end a life.

There is a second breastplate in Scripture. The high priest wore the breastpiece of judgment, set with stones engraved with the names of the tribes of Israel, and he carried those names on his heart when he went in before YHWH (Exodus 28:29). The Hebrew words differ. Isaiah uses shiryon, body armor, and Exodus uses choshen, the priestly breastpiece. But both sit over the heart. One guards it. The other carries the people on it.
The Word Behind It

The Hebrew word for righteousness is tsedaqah: what is right and straight, measured by YHWH's standard, not ours. Abraham believed YHWH, and He counted it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6). That same Abraham obeyed His voice and kept His commandments, statutes, and instructions (Genesis 26:5).
Righteousness begins as a gift received by faith, and it shows up as a life that does what is right (1 John 3:7).
Walking It Out

Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life (Proverbs 4:23). The enemy rarely gets through with one big blow. He works through small cracks: a compromise excused, a sin hidden, a grudge kept. Guilt and shame pour in through those cracks until a believer feels too dirty to stand.

The answer is not trying harder to look clean. It is putting on what Yahshua already won, and then walking in His instructions. When you fall, run to Him instead of away from Him. If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous to forgive us (1 John 1:9).

blocks.title: Forgiveness And The Breastplate
blocks.v: Unforgiveness is one of the widest cracks in the armor. Yahshua tied our forgiveness to our forgiving others (Matthew 6:14-15).
Pride holds the grudge in place. Humility lets it go. Forgiveness closes the gap.
For Reflection

items: What small compromise have you been excusing? Is there sin you are hiding instead of bringing into the light?
Who are you still holding a grudge against?

sections.heading: The Shoes of the Good News of Peace

blocks.v: and having fitted your feet with the preparation of the Good News of peace;
Where Paul Got It
Isaiah saw a messenger crossing the mountains toward Jerusalem with the news everyone had been waiting for.
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of good, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, Your Elohim reigns!

Paul quotes this verse in Romans 10:15 for everyone who carries the message. Earlier in Ephesians he told us what that peace is. Yahshua Himself is our peace. He made the two one, broke down the middle wall that divided them, and came preaching peace to those who were far off and to those who were near (Ephesians 2:14-17, echoing Isaiah
57:19). The good news of peace is the news of a divided people made one under one King.

Paul ties peace to feet one more time: the Elohim of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet (Romans 16:20). That reaches back to the first promise, that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15).
The Soldier Paul Saw

Roman soldiers wore heavy military sandal boots called caligae, with thick leather soles studded with iron hobnails. Those nails bit into the ground and gave grip on rough terrain, and the boots were built for long marches. In close fighting, the man who lost his footing was the man in danger.
The Word Behind It

Paul's word for preparation is hetoimasia: readiness, being prepared to move. The Greek translation of the Old Testament uses the same word in Psalm 89:14 (88:15 in Greek numbering), where righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne. Paul's word carries both ideas: ready to move, and planted on solid ground.
The Hebrew word for peace is shalom, from a root meaning whole or complete. Shalom is not just the absence of fighting. It is everything in its right place.
Walking It Out

Peace is not the absence of battle. It is the ground you stand on in the middle of one. Having been justified by faith, we have peace with Elohim (Romans 5:1), and His peace guards our hearts and our thoughts (Philippians 4:6-7). When your footing is settled, the storm can hit without knocking you down.

These shoes also point outward. As much as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone (Romans 12:18). Blessed are the peacemakers (Matthew 5:9). Unforgiveness makes the ground slippery, and it is hard to carry good news of peace to someone you refuse to release. And shoes are made for walking: be ready to give an answer for the hope that is in you (1 Peter 3:15).

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: You do not fight for peace with Elohim. You fight from it. Yahshua already made it.
For Reflection

items: What knocks you off your footing most easily?
Who do you need to make peace with?
Where might Yahshua be sending you with the good news this week?

blocks.v: above all, taking up the shield of faith, with which you will be able to quench all the fiery darts of the evil one.
Where Paul Got It

Long before Paul, YHWH told Abram, I am your shield (Genesis 15:1). Psalm 91:4 says His faithfulness is your shield, and the Hebrew word there is amitto, from emet, the same word for truth we met at the belt. Proverbs 30:5 says every word of Elohim is tested, and He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
So the shield is not your faith as a feeling. The shield is His faithfulness, and your faith is the hand that lifts it.
The Soldier Paul Saw

Paul's Greek word for shield is thureos, related to thura, the word for door. This was not a small round shield. It was the large, curved Roman scutum, big enough to cover most of a man's body. The Greek historian Polybius described it as two layers of wood glued together, covered with canvas and then calfskin, with iron edging.

Ancient armies did shoot arrows wrapped in burning material. A soldier could crouch behind his scutum, and a unit could lock shields together over their heads and sides in a formation called the testudo, the tortoise, so the whole group was covered at once.
The Word Behind It

The Greek word for faith is pistis. It means trust, and it also means faithfulness. The Hebrew idea behind it is emunah, from the same root as emet. The righteous will live by his faith (Habakkuk 2:4), and Paul quotes that verse more than once. In Scripture, faith is not a mood. It is steady trust that keeps holding on.
The phrase translated above all is often understood as in addition to all these. The shield is taken up along with every other piece, in every situation.
Walking It Out

Fiery darts come fast and without warning: a sudden doubt, a wave of fear, an accusation, a temptation, a thought that is not yours. Psalm 64:3 describes enemies who aim bitter words like arrows. You do not have to stop and argue with every one. You lift the shield and set what YHWH has said and done between you and the dart.

Feed your faith, because faith comes by hearing the word (Romans 10:17). Rehearse His faithfulness in your own story, because the saints overcame by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony (Revelation 12:11). And do not fight alone. Stay close to believers who will stand with you (Hebrews 10:24-25).

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: A lone shield covers one man. Locked shields cover a whole unit. The shield was never meant to be carried in isolation.
For Reflection

items: Which fiery dart hits you most often?
Name three times YHWH proved faithful to you.
Who are you standing shoulder to shoulder with right now?

blocks.v: And take the helmet of salvation,
Where Paul Got It

We met this helmet in Isaiah 59:17, on the head of YHWH as He came to rescue His people. Paul did not only borrow the idea. The words he uses for helmet of salvation match the words of the Greek translation of Isaiah in that verse.

Paul uses the helmet again in 1 Thessalonians 5:8, where he calls it the hope of salvation. He writes that just after describing the day Yahshua returns at the trumpet and the dead are raised (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17). The helmet looks forward.
The Soldier Paul Saw

The Roman helmet, the galea, was made of bronze or iron, with hinged cheek pieces to protect the face and a guard at the back to protect the neck. A soldier could survive many wounds, but a blow to the head was often the end.
The Word Behind It

The Hebrew word for salvation in Isaiah 59:17 is yeshuah: rescue, deliverance, victory. It is the word Moses used at the Red Sea when he told Israel to stand still and see the salvation of YHWH (Exodus 14:13). The name Yahshua is built on the same root, and the angel said He would save His people from their sins (Matthew 1:21).
When you put on the helmet of salvation, you are covering your mind with what His name means.
Walking It Out

The mind is where many battles are won or lost. The enemy whispers: you are still guilty, nothing will ever change, Elohim is done with you. Those thoughts aim straight at the head. The helmet answers with three truths.

You have been rescued. There is no condemnation for those who are in Messiah Yahshua (Romans 8:1). You are being delivered. You are transformed by the renewing of your mind (Romans 12:2). You will be raised. Your future is secure at His return.

So take every thought captive to the obedience of Messiah (2 Corinthians 10:5). When a thought comes, check it against the word. If it does not line up, it does not stay. Then fill that space with whatever is true, honorable, pure, and lovely (Philippians 4:8).

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: Condemnation is aimed at the head because a wounded mind stops fighting. Salvation is the covering that answers it.
For Reflection

items: What thought keeps coming back to you?
Does it line up with what Scripture says?
How does the hope of His return change how you think today?

blocks.v: and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of Elohim;
Where Paul Got It

In Scripture, this sword comes out of a mouth. YHWH made His Servant's mouth like a sharp sword (Isaiah 49:2). The Branch strikes the earth with the rod of His mouth and slays the wicked with the breath of His lips (Isaiah 11:4), the same chapter where we found the belt. YHWH says He cut down the rebellious by the words of His mouth (Hosea 6:5). And when John saw Yahshua return, a sharp sword came out of His mouth (Revelation 19:15).
The sword of the Spirit is the word spoken.
The Soldier Paul Saw

Paul's word for sword is machaira, a shorter blade suited to close fighting, like the Roman gladius. A later Roman writer, Vegetius, described recruits practicing strikes against a wooden post with training weapons heavier than real ones, so the real sword felt light in battle.
The Word Behind It
Paul had two common Greek words for word: logos and rhema. He chose rhema, which usually means a spoken word. Yahshua used the same word in the wilderness.
It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of Elohim's mouth.
Notice where Yahshua went every time. All three answers came from Deuteronomy (8:3, 6:16, 6:13). He fought with Torah, and He spoke it out loud.
Notice something else. The enemy quoted Scripture too, pulling Psalm 91 out of its setting (Matthew 4:6). Knowing verses is not enough. We have to know what they mean in context.
Walking It Out

The sword is the one piece made for striking, but it only works in your hand, not on the shelf. Read it. Hide it in your heart so it is there when you need it (Psalm 119:11). Then speak it when the attack comes, the way Yahshua did.

The word of Elohim is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, and it discerns the thoughts of the heart (Hebrews 4:12). That means it cuts us first. Let it correct you before you swing it at anything else. And train before the battle. The recruit who practiced with the heavy weapon was ready when it counted.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: Three temptations. Three answers. Every one from the instructions of YHWH, and every one spoken. The sword works when it is in the mouth.
For Reflection

items: What verse would you reach for in your biggest battle right now?
Do you know that verse in its context?
What has the word corrected in you lately?

blocks.v: with all prayer and requests, praying at all times in the Spirit, and being watchful to this end in all perseverance and requests for all the saints:
Where Paul Got It

When Amalek attacked Israel, Joshua fought in the valley while Moses stood on the hill with his hands raised. As long as Moses' hands were up, Israel prevailed. When they dropped, Amalek prevailed. So Aaron and Hur held his hands up until sunset, and the battle was won (Exodus 17:8-13). The fight in the valley and the prayer on the hill were one battle.

Isaiah 62:6 speaks of watchmen YHWH set on the walls of Jerusalem who would never be silent day or night. In Gethsemane, Yahshua told His disciples to watch and pray so they would not enter into temptation (Matthew 26:41).
The Soldier Paul Saw

A Roman camp kept watch through the night in shifts. Polybius describes a watchword passed through the camp each night, and harsh punishment, even death, for a sentry who failed his watch. Armor did a sleeping soldier no good.
The Word Behind It

The Greek word for being watchful is agrypneo, which literally means to stay awake, to go without sleep. The word for requests is deesis, specific needs brought before Elohim. This is not vague prayer. It is alert, specific, and it keeps going.
Then read the next two verses. Paul, in chains, asked them to pray for him. He did not ask for release. He asked for boldness to open his mouth and make the good news known (Ephesians 6:19-20).
Walking It Out

Prayer is how a believer puts on every other piece and stays in contact with the Commander. It is relationship, not ritual. Start the morning by putting on each piece in prayer. Talk to Him through the day in short, honest words. End the night with Him.
And remember Moses. Someone you know is fighting in the valley right now. Be the one who holds up their hands. Pray for the saints by name, and ask others to pray for you.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: Prayer is not a seventh piece of armor. It is how you put on the other six.
For Reflection

items: Who is in the valley right now that you can hold up in prayer? Is your prayer life steady, or mostly saved for a crisis?
What would it look like to pray for boldness instead of escape?

blocks.v: Popular teaching on the armor often repeats details that do not hold up. Where Scripture and history stop speaking, we should not fill the gap and call it fact. Here is what this study deliberately left out or held loosely.
Soaked shields. It is often said Roman soldiers soaked their shields in water before battle to put out flaming arrows. We could not find an ancient source that says this, so it is not taught here.

items: One kind of armor. Many teachings picture every soldier in segmented iron plate. Mail armor was at least as common in Paul's day.
Famous quotes. Devotional material often attaches quotes to well known teachers without any source. Scripture is the stronger witness, so this study stays with it.
Where Paul wrote from. Ephesians says Paul was in chains, and Rome is the traditional setting, but the letter does not name the city. We hold that loosely.

blocks.v: One piece a day. Small enough to actually do.
Belt. Write down one lie you have been believing and one verse that answers it. Read the verse out loud morning and
night.
Breastplate. Ask Yahshua to show you one small compromise you have been excusing. Confess it and take one step to
close that crack.
Shoes. Ask Him to bring to mind one person you need to make peace with. Take one step: a prayer of release, a text, or a
call.
Shield. Write down three times YHWH was faithful to you, and share one of them with someone.
Helmet. Catch one thought that keeps coming back. Find a verse that answers it and replace the thought every time it
returns.
Sword. Pick your biggest battle, find one verse that speaks to it, memorize it, and say it out loud when that battle shows
up.
Prayer. Choose one person to hold up in prayer every day, and start each morning by praying through the full armor.

16:20; Ephesians 2:14-17; Philippians 4:6-7; 1 Peter 3:15
