blocks.title: Putting On The Armor
blocks.v: Yahshua, I come to You as my Commander. Today I put on Your whole armor. I buckle on Your truth. I put on Your righteousness over my heart. I stand in Your peace, ready to go where You send me. I lift the shield of faith against every fiery dart. I cover my mind with Your salvation. I take up Your word as my sword. Keep me awake and watchful. Teach me to pray at all times, not only in crisis. Show me who to hold up in prayer today, and give me boldness to speak Your good news. Amen.

topics.title: Sex Before Marriage
topics.subtitle: What YHWH Calls It, What It Joins, and the Way Back
topics.note: A Teaching Study on 1 Corinthians 6:13-20 Scripture quoted from the World English Bible (WEB), divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai, with Yahshua and Messiah in place of Jesus and Christ. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Our culture treats sex before marriage as normal, and many believers have quietly accepted the claim that the Bible never actually forbids it. The words YHWH chose say otherwise. The Greek, the Hebrew, and His own instructions all point the same direction.

Sex was designed to seal a covenant, not to test one. Outside of covenant it still joins two people, and that is exactly why it does so much damage. But this study does not end in condemnation. It ends in freedom.

blocks.title: How This Study Works
blocks.v: Each section sets out what the text says, the Hebrew or Greek words behind it, and what it means for how we walk. Where a common teaching phrase is not found in Scripture, the study says so plainly and shows what the text does say. Each section closes with questions for reflection or discussion.

Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods, but Elohim will bring to nothing both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for Adonai; and Adonai for the body. Now Elohim raised up Adonai, and will also raise us up by his power. Don't you know that your bodies are members of Messiah? Shall I then take the members of Messiah and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be! Or don't you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, The two, he says, will become one flesh. But he who is joined to Adonai is one spirit. Flee sexual immorality! Every sin that a man does is outside the body, but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body. Or don't you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from Elohim? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify Elohim in your body and in your spirit, which are Elohim's.

Paul wrote this to believers in Corinth, a port city known across the Roman world for its sexual looseness. Some of them had decided that what they did with their bodies did not touch their spirits. Paul answers that the body belongs to Adonai, that sex joins two people whether they intend it or not, and that the price already paid for them settles who owns their bodies.
The most common objection is that Scripture condemns adultery, but never says a word about two single people who love each other. The answer starts with the word the Apostles actually used.
The Word Behind It

The Greek word is porneia (G4202), usually translated "fornication" or "sexual immorality." It comes from pornē (G4204), a harlot, and the lexicons trace that back to pernēmi, "to sell." At its root, porneia is intimacy pulled out of covenant and treated as a transaction.
Adultery has its own Greek word, moicheia (G3430). When Yahshua listed what comes out of a defiled heart, He named the two separately:
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.
If porneia only meant cheating on a spouse, Yahshua would not have needed two words in the same breath. The writer of Hebrews does the same thing:
Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the bed be undefiled; but Elohim will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
Two groups again: the pornos (G4205), the sexually immoral, and the moichos (G3432), the adulterer. The first group is broader than the second, and it includes sex before marriage.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: Porneia is the umbrella. Adultery is one kind of sexual sin; sex outside of marriage in any form, including before it, falls under porneia. Scripture names it, and Elohim says He will judge it.
Paul says the same thing as a direct instruction:

For this is the will of Elohim: your sanctification, that you abstain from sexual immorality, that each one of you know how to control his own body in sanctification and honor, not in the passion of lust, even as the Gentiles who don't know Elohim,
The word for sanctification is hagiasmos (G38), being set apart. Sexual purity is not a side issue for a believer. Paul calls it the will of Elohim.
For Reflection

items: Where did you first hear that the Bible does not forbid sex before marriage?
Why do you think Yahshua and the writer of Hebrews kept the two words separate?

blocks.v: The instructions of YHWH use the Hebrew word zanah (H2181), to commit harlotry or fornication. The clearest case of how He applies it to an unmarried woman is in Deuteronomy 22.
In Deuteronomy 22:13-21, a husband accuses his new bride of not having been a virgin. If the charge is false, he is fined and may never divorce her. If it is true, the text says:

then they shall bring out the young lady to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death with stones, because she has done folly in Israel, to play the prostitute in her father's house. So you shall remove the evil from among you.

"Play the prostitute" is zanah. This woman was not married when it happened. She was not cheating on anyone. And the instructions still call it harlotry and folly in Israel. That settles how YHWH defines sex before marriage.

blocks.title: What This Does Not Mean
blocks.v: The death penalty in this passage was carried out by Israel's courts, in the land, on the testimony of witnesses. This study is not teaching that anyone should be stoned today. It is showing how YHWH defines the act. The penalty tells you how seriously He takes it; the rest of Scripture tells you where mercy is found.
For Reflection

items: Does it surprise you that Deuteronomy uses the word for harlotry about an unmarried woman?
Why would YHWH treat something done "in her father's house" as a matter for the whole community?

sections.heading: You Open It, You Bought It

blocks.v: Everyone knows how it works at the grocery store. You can pick something up and read the label. But once you tear the package open and start eating, you are not a shopper anymore. You are paying for it. YHWH wrote that principle into His instructions, and He wrote it to protect the woman.

If a man entices a virgin who isn't pledged to be married, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his wife. If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
The Words Behind It

"Virgin" is bethulah (H1330). "Entices" is pathah (H6601), to persuade, to sweet talk, even to deceive. This is the man who says the covenant is only a piece of paper. "Dowry" is mohar (H4119), the bride-price.

Notice what the instruction does. The man pays the full bride-price whether or not he gets to marry her. Her father could refuse the marriage altogether, and the man still paid. The cost landed on him, not on her.
Deuteronomy adds a second case:

If a man finds a lady who is a virgin, who is not pledged to be married, grabs her and lies with her, and they are found, then the man who lay with her shall give to the lady's father fifty shekels of silver. She shall be his wife, because he has humbled her. He may not put her away all his days.

"Grabs" is taphas (H8610), to seize or take hold of. "Humbled" is anah (H6031), to afflict, to bring low, to violate. YHWH saw what the act did to her, and He made sure the man could never use her and walk away. No divorce, all his days.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: The analogy works because of who it protects. The woman is not the product in this picture. The instruction made sure no man could open what he was not willing to pay for, and could never walk away from what he took.
For Reflection

items: What does it say about YHWH that the cost of this sin fell on the one who pursued it?
How does the phrase "it is just a piece of paper" sound after reading the word pathah?

blocks.v: Or don't you know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from Elohim? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify Elohim in your body and in your spirit, which are Elohim's.

The Greek word for "bought" is agorazō (G59), from agora (G58), the marketplace. It is the everyday word for buying something in the market square. Paul takes the grocery store picture and turns it around. You are not the shopper in this story. You have already been purchased, and the price was the blood of Yahshua.

"Temple" is naos (G3485), not the general word for the temple grounds but the word for the inner sanctuary, the dwelling place itself. Your body is where the Spirit of Elohim lives. That is why Paul can say the body is not for sexual immorality, but for Adonai, and Adonai for the body (1 Corinthians 6:13).
Your body is not yours to hand out. It belongs to the One who paid for it.
For Reflection

items: How does knowing you were bought change the question "what is wrong with it if we love each other?"
What would it look like this week to glorify Elohim in your body?

blocks.v: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
"Join" is dabaq (H1692), to cling, to stick fast, to be glued together. That is YHWH's design: two lives fused into one, inside of covenant.
Now watch the same word appear where there was no covenant at all. Shechem took Dinah, lay with her, and humbled her, and right after, Scripture says:
His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.

"Soul" is nephesh (H5315), and "joined" is dabaq again. The act created a bond in him, with no covenant, no consent from her, and no blessing from her father. The bond did not make it right. It made the damage worse, and the chapter ends with bloodshed (Genesis 34:25).
Paul says the same thing in the Greek:
Or don't you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, The two, he says, will become one flesh. But he who is joined to Adonai is one spirit.

"Joined" is kollaō (G2853), to glue or cement together. Paul quotes Genesis 2:24 about a man and a prostitute. Sex outside of marriage does not escape the one flesh reality. It sets that reality in motion with someone you have no covenant with. And notice verse 17: the same verb describes being joined to Adonai. He designed us to be joined, to Him first and to one spouse in covenant.

blocks.title: Where Scripture Stops
blocks.v: The phrase "soul tie" is not found in Scripture. It is a teaching term. What Scripture does show is the reality behind it: dabaq in Genesis 34:3, a soul clinging after the act, and kollaō in 1 Corinthians 6:16, two people glued into one body. Teach the verses, and let the term stay a term.
For Reflection

items: Why do you think people often feel bound to someone they know was not good for them?
What does verse 17 tell you about what you were actually made to be joined to?

sections.heading: A Sin Against Your Own Body

blocks.v: Flee sexual immorality! Every sin that a man does is outside the body, but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

"Flee" is pheugō (G5343), to run for your life. It is the word used when Joseph was told to flee into Egypt with the child (Matthew 2:13). Paul does not tell them to manage it, negotiate with it, or see how close they can get. He tells them to run. Joseph is the picture: when Potiphar's wife grabbed his garment, he left it in her hand and ran out of the house (Genesis 39:12).
Paul says this sin is different because it is committed against your own body, the very place the Spirit dwells. It is not only something you do. It is something done to the temple.
What About Open Doors?
Scripture does not use the phrase "open door" for this, but it does give a principle:
and don't give place to the devil.

"Place" is topos (G5117), a spot, a piece of ground. In context Paul is talking about anger, not sex, so this is a principle and not a proof text. But it runs through all of Scripture: sin that is practiced and not confessed hands the enemy ground to stand on. In deliverance ministry, bonds from past relationships are often the ground that has to be taken back before a marriage can be whole.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: Every other sin a man commits is outside the body. This one is committed in the temple itself. That is why the instruction is not "be careful." It is "run."
For Reflection

items: What situations do you need to run from instead of trying to stand in? Is there ground in your life that you have handed over and never taken back?

blocks.v: Most people reading this have a past. YHWH did not give the truth to crush anyone. He gave it so we could be free. Look at what Paul says right after he lists the sexually immoral among those who will not inherit the Kingdom:
Some of you were such, but you were washed. But you were sanctified. But you were justified in the name of Adonai Yahshua, and in the Spirit of our Elohim.
"Some of you were such." That is past tense. The people in Corinth had lived in porneia, and Yahshua washed them. What He did for them, He will do for you. Here is what walking out of it looks like.
1. Call It What YHWH Calls It
Not a mistake, not "we were in love," but sin. Confession means agreeing with Elohim about what it was.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
2. Bring It Into the Light
Shame lives in secret. It loses its power in the light.
Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed.
3. Renounce the Bond

Speak it out loud in the name of Yahshua: you are no longer joined to that person, and you take back every piece of ground you handed the enemy. Scripture gives no ritual for this, and none is needed. It is confession, repentance, and a clear declaration of whose you are.
4. Forgive
Forgive the one who pressured or used you, and receive the forgiveness Yahshua already paid for. Unforgiveness keeps the chain attached. Forgiveness is the root of deliverance.
5. Walk as a New Creation
Therefore if anyone is in Messiah, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

blocks.title: Right Where You Are
blocks.v: If you are single: you are not damaged goods. Guard what He restored. The Song of Songs says three times that love should not be stirred up or awakened until it so desires (Song of Songs 2:7, 3:5, 8:4).
If you are living together: Paul gives the answer plainly. It is better to marry than to burn (1 Corinthians 7:9). Make the covenant, or step back until you can.
If you are married and carrying bonds from before: pray through this together. YHWH restores marriages. That is His design, and it is what this ministry exists for.
For Reflection

items: Which of the five steps is hardest for you, and why?
Who is one trusted person you could bring this into the light with?

blocks.v: Primary text: 1 Corinthians 6:12-20 Porneia named apart from adultery: Matthew 15:19; Mark 7:21-22; Hebrews 13:4; Galatians 5:19 The will of Elohim: 1 Thessalonians 4:3-8; Romans 12:1
Zanah before marriage: Deuteronomy 22:13-21

The man pays: Exodus 22:16-17; Deuteronomy 22:28-29 Bought with a price: 1 Corinthians 6:19-20; 1 Corinthians 7:23; 1 Peter 1:18-19 One flesh: Genesis 2:24; Genesis 34:3; Matthew 19:5-6; 1 Corinthians 6:16-17; Ephesians 5:31 Flee: 1 Corinthians 6:18; Genesis 39:12; 2 Timothy 2:22 Giving ground: Ephesians 4:27; James 4:7 Washed and made new: 1 Corinthians 6:11; 1 John 1:9; James 5:16; 2 Corinthians 5:17 Wait for it: Song of Songs 2:7, 3:5, 8:4; 1 Corinthians 7:2, 7:9

blocks.title: Putting It Into Prayer
blocks.v: Yahshua, You bought me with Your own blood, and my body belongs to You. I confess every place I gave myself outside of covenant, and I call it what You call it. Wash me. In Your name I renounce every bond I formed outside of Your design, and I take back every piece of ground I handed the enemy. I forgive those who used me, and I receive Your forgiveness. Make me new. Teach me to flee, to wait, and to honor You in my body. Amen.

topics.title: One Flesh, One Bride
topics.subtitle: What Scripture Really Says About Polygamy
topics.note: A Teaching Study on Genesis 2:24 and Matthew 19:4-8 Scripture quoted from the World English Bible (WEB), divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai, with Yahshua and Messiah in place of Jesus and Christ. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Abraham, Jacob, David, and Solomon all had more than one wife, and some people conclude that YHWH must be fine with it. Scripture tells a different story. It records polygamy honestly, regulates it, and then shows us what it did to every household whose story it tells in detail.
What YHWH regulates is not always what YHWH designed. His design has been one man and one woman from the garden, and it points to one Bridegroom and His one bride.

blocks.title: How This Study Works
blocks.v: We start with the design, then look at how the instructions handle polygamy, then walk through the households Scripture lets us see, then answer the hard verses head on. Where Scripture does not say something in so many words, this study says so plainly. Each section closes with questions for reflection or discussion.
Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.

The Hebrew is ishto, "his wife," singular. "Join" is dabaq (H1692), to cling, to be glued together. One man leaves, one man clings, to one woman, and the two become one flesh. Adam was not given a second Eve, and Noah took one wife into the ark, as did each of his three sons (Genesis 7:13).
When the Pharisees tested Yahshua about marriage, He did not start with Abraham or David. He went back to Eden:

He answered, Haven't you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?' So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore Elohim has joined together, don't let man tear apart.

In Matthew's Greek, Yahshua quotes the verse as "the two shall become one flesh," the same wording found in the Greek translation of Genesis. Then He adds His own commentary: "they are no more two, but one flesh." The number in the design is two becoming one.
For Reflection

items: Why do you think Yahshua answered a question about marriage by going back to the beginning?
What does "the two shall become one" leave room for, and what does it not?

blocks.v: In the same conversation, the Pharisees asked why Moses allowed divorce. Yahshua's answer gives us a principle:
He said to them, Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.

Yahshua was answering a question about divorce there, not polygamy. But He showed that YHWH sometimes gave instructions to limit the damage of hard hearts, and that those instructions do not overrule the design "from the beginning." The instructions about polygamy fit that pattern.
If he takes another wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.
This protects the first wife. A man who takes another wife may not cut her food, her clothing, or her marital rights.
If a man has two wives, the one beloved and the other hated, and they have borne him children, both the beloved and the hated, and if the firstborn son is hers who was hated,

This protects the firstborn son of the wife who is not loved. Look at what the instruction assumes: in a house with two wives, one ends up loved, ahav (H157), and the other hated, sane (H8130). The instruction does not bless the arrangement. It puts a guardrail on the damage.
YHWH also set limits:
You shall not take a wife in addition to her sister, to be a rival, to uncover her nakedness, while her sister is still alive.
He shall not multiply wives to himself, that his heart not turn away. He shall not greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

blocks.title: Where Scripture Stops
blocks.v: There is no verse in the instructions that says, in so many words, "a man shall have only one wife." Honesty requires saying that. The case against polygamy rests on the design in Genesis 2, Yahshua's appeal to "the beginning," the way the instructions treat it as damage to be limited, the record of every household Scripture shows us, and the standard the Apostles set. Taken together, that is a strong case, and it is the one this study makes.
For Reflection

items: Can you think of other things YHWH regulated that He never called good?
Why would Deuteronomy assume one wife will be "hated"?

sections.heading: The Hebrew Word for a Second Wife

blocks.v: The word "rival" in Leviticus 18:18 is tsarar (H6887), to vex, to show hostility, to be an adversary. From that same root comes tsarah, the word Scripture uses for a co-wife. It is spelled exactly like tsarah (H6869), the ordinary word for trouble and distress.
You can see it in Hannah's story. Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and Peninnah had children while Hannah had none:
Her rival provoked her severely, to irritate her, because YHWH had shut up her womb.
"Her rival" is tsaratah, her co-wife. It went on year after year, until Hannah wept and would not eat (1 Samuel 1:7).

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: The Hebrew language itself tells you what a second wife brings into a home. The word for her is spelled the same as the word for trouble.
For Reflection

items: What does it tell you that the language of Scripture has a word for a rival wife at all?

blocks.v: Scripture does not hide the lives of its heroes. It shows us what happened in their homes. Here is every household with multiple wives whose story it tells in any detail.
Lamech

The first man recorded with two wives was Lamech, of the line of Cain (Genesis 4:19). His next recorded words are a boast to both wives that he killed a man for wounding him (Genesis 4:23). That is where polygamy enters the story.
Abraham

Sarai gave Hagar to Abram "to be his wife" (Genesis 16:3). As soon as Hagar conceived, she despised Sarai. Sarai blamed Abram, dealt harshly with Hagar, and Hagar ran into the wilderness (Genesis 16:4-6). The rivalry carried into the next generation with Ishmael and Isaac (Genesis 21:9-10).
Esau
When Esau was forty years old, he took as wife Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite. They grieved Isaac's and Rebekah's spirits.
Jacob

Leah, Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah turned his tents into a competition. "Rachel envied her sister" (Genesis 30:1). When Bilhah bore a son, Rachel named him Naphtali and said she had wrestled with her sister and prevailed (Genesis 30:8). Jacob loved Rachel's son Joseph more than the others, and the sons of the other mothers hated Joseph and sold him into slavery (Genesis 37:3-4, 28).
Elkanah
Peninnah provoked Hannah year after year (1 Samuel 1:6-7), as we saw above.
Gideon
Gideon had seventy sons conceived from his body, for he had many wives. His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
After Gideon died, Abimelech, the son of the concubine, killed his brothers, seventy persons, on one stone. Only Jotham, the youngest, escaped by hiding (Judges 9:5).
David

David took wife after wife, and six sons were born to him in Hebron by six different wives (2 Samuel 3:2-5). His children from different mothers tore his house apart. Amnon violated his half sister Tamar. Her full brother Absalom killed Amnon, then rose up against his own father, and went in to his father's concubines on the roof in the sight of all Israel (2 Samuel 13; 15; 16:22). Later Adonijah, son of yet another wife, tried to seize the throne (1 Kings 1:5).
Solomon

He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines. His wives turned his heart away. When Solomon was old, his wives turned away his heart after other gods; and his heart was not perfect with YHWH his Elohim, as the heart of David his father was.
Solomon broke Deuteronomy 17:17 to the letter, and it happened exactly as the instruction warned: his heart turned away. YHWH told him the kingdom would be torn from his house (1 Kings 11:11).

blocks.title: Being Fair To The Text
blocks.v: Scripture also names men such as Ashhur (1 Chronicles 4:5) and Caleb (1 Chronicles 2:18-19, 46-48) with more than one wife or concubine, and tells us nothing about their homes. So the honest claim is not that every polygamist suffered for it. It is that every time Scripture lets us see inside such a house, we find jealousy, rivalry, favoritism, and broken children, and it never once holds one up as the model to follow.
For Reflection

items: Which of these households do you think suffered the most, and why?
Why would Scripture record these stories in so much detail?

blocks.v: Two passages are often used to argue that YHWH approved of polygamy. Both deserve a straight answer.
2 Samuel 12:8

I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that would have been too little, I would have added to you many more such things.

Read the context. Nathan has just told David a parable about a rich man with many flocks and a poor man who had nothing but "one little ewe lamb" (2 Samuel 12:3). In that culture a new king inherited the royal household of the old one, and YHWH is reminding David that He gave him everything: the throne, the house, the kingdom. David still stole a man's only wife. Then comes the sentence:
Now therefore the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised me, and have taken Uriah the Hittite's wife to be your wife.

This verse shows YHWH working through the customs of that day to rebuke David. It is a charge of ingratitude, not a blessing on a harem, and it never rewrites Genesis 2. Within a few chapters, the judgment in verse 11 was carried out on the roof of David's own house (2 Samuel 16:22).
Ezekiel 23 and Jeremiah 3

In these chapters YHWH describes Himself as husband to two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, Samaria and Jerusalem, the house of Israel and the house of Judah. But those two were one people, one nation, torn in two by sin after Solomon (1 Kings 12). The split was the tragedy, not the design. And YHWH's promise is to put it back together:
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will be king to them all. They will no longer be two nations. They won't be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.
Even here, His plan ends with one.
For Reflection

items: Why is it important to read 2 Samuel 12:8 together with verses 3 and 10?
How does Ezekiel 37 change the way you read Ezekiel 23?

blocks.v: But, because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
Each man, his own wife. Each woman, her own husband. When Paul set the standard for leaders in the assembly, he wrote:
The overseer therefore must be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, sensible, modest, hospitable, good at teaching;
In the Greek this is mias gunaikos andra, literally "a one woman man" (also Titus 1:6). Those leaders were the example the whole assembly was called to follow (1 Corinthians 11:1).
And here is why it matters so much. Paul quotes Genesis 2:24 and then tells us what it has been pointing to all along:
For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will be joined to his wife. The two will become one flesh. This mystery is great, but I speak concerning Messiah and of the assembly.
Marriage is a living picture of Yahshua and His people. He does not have a collection of brides:
For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.v: One Bridegroom. One bride. Every marriage is meant to preach that message, from the garden to the wedding of the Lamb.
For Reflection

items: What does your marriage, or the marriage you hope for, preach about Yahshua and His bride?

blocks.v: Few people reading this are weighing a second wife. But the same pull shows up in other forms: a divided heart, an emotional affair, a marriage where someone else holds the place that belongs to a spouse.

If you are married: guard the "one." Let no one else, in person or on a screen, hold a place in your heart that belongs to your spouse. Cling, dabaq, to one. If you come from a divided house: the rivalry you grew up in is not your inheritance. Forgive, and ask Yahshua to heal what the division did to you. Joseph's story ended in reconciliation (Genesis 45:4-15). If someone uses the patriarchs to justify it: point them back to "the beginning," to Hannah's tears, to Solomon's turned heart, and to the one bride Yahshua is coming for.

The design: Genesis 2:18-24; Genesis 7:13; Malachi 2:14-15; Matthew 19:4-6; Mark 10:6-9 Regulated, not designed: Matthew 19:8; Exodus 21:10; Deuteronomy 21:15-17 Limits: Leviticus 18:18; Deuteronomy 17:17
The rival wife: 1 Samuel 1:2-7

Named without a story: 1 Chronicles 2:18-19, 46-48; 1 Chronicles 4:5 The hard verses: 2 Samuel 12:1-11; Ezekiel 23; Jeremiah 3:6-10; Ezekiel 37:15-22 One bride: 1 Corinthians 7:2-4; 1 Timothy 3:2; Titus 1:6; Ephesians 5:22-33; Revelation 19:7-9

blocks.title: Putting It Into Prayer
blocks.v: Yahshua, You are the Bridegroom, and You are coming for one bride. Thank You that Your design has never changed. Make my heart undivided toward You. Guard my marriage, or the marriage You have for me, and teach me to cling to one. Heal every place where division and rivalry wounded my family, and make us one again, the way You promised to make Your people one. Amen.

topics.title: My Testimony
topics.lede: How YHWH took a man out of gangs, jail, and addiction, and made him a husband and a father.
topics.note: Michael Ben Yah. All Scripture from the World English Bible, divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai.

blocks.v: I want to step back and explain how all of this started.

I grew up with a wonderful mother who took me to church and taught me the things of YHWH. But even with that foundation, I carried pain and unforgiveness in my heart because I grew up in a divorced and broken home.

As a teenager I drifted into gangs and criminal activity. The trauma I went through did not stay trauma. It turned into bitterness and unforgiveness, and that is what opened the doors. Unforgiveness gives the enemy legal ground in your life, and once he has ground he does not sit still with it. (Ephesians 4:26-27, Hebrews 12:15)

Those open doors led me into bad relationships, addictions, and destructive patterns. Deep down I always wanted to do what was right. I just did not know that demons were influencing me, and I would not know it until the day I was delivered.
I was using drugs, drinking heavily, fornicating, and going in and out of jail. That road was leading straight to death.

Even then, YHWH had His hand on me. He guided me into the Army, and the Army gave me the first sense of direction I ever had that was not street life. It taught me discipline. It taught me leadership. It showed me there was a better path to live. And that was where I first started to know that I was lost and that I needed Yahshua.
I started a family. That marriage ended in divorce in 2009, from immaturity on my part and unfaithfulness on hers, and their mother took the children.

My twenties and thirties were full of mistakes. I struggled to stay away from drugs and alcohol, and I turned back to them every time the pain got too heavy. My mom had planted faith in me, but I did not truly believe there was a spiritual realm. Still, I started going to church regularly, and I kept hearing the same three words over and over: demons, deliverance, unforgiveness.
The weekend of December 22, 2011, I attended an Encounter at Tarpley, a three day deliverance event hosted by one of the churches I was attending. I was twenty nine years old.

The first two days were prayer, reflection, and writing down traumas and hidden hurts so we could forgive the people who wounded us. I asked YHWH to reveal the unforgiveness buried deep inside my heart, and He did. Some of what He brought up were things I did not even remember. That is where the real healing started. I wrote letters and I forgave people I had been holding in my heart for years. (Matthew 18:34-35)

The whole time there was praise and worship going up, inviting His presence into the atmosphere. Somewhere in that process I began to understand that I needed deliverance. Demons had a hold on my life and they were influencing my decisions and my behavior.

The third day was the deliverance session. By then Yah had already shown me that the root of all of it was unforgiveness, and that I had to release it if I wanted to be healed and walk the new path with Him that I had always wanted deep down.

The pastor was leading a mass deliverance. At some point he must have seen that I had a demon, because he and the team came straight over, surrounded me, and started praying. When he commanded the demon to come out, I was told to breathe out.

When I did, I felt something leave my body. It is hard to explain to somebody who has never been through it. I immediately felt lighter, like an oppressive force I had been carrying my whole life had just been lifted off of me.
Right there I declared Yahshua as my Lord and Savior and invited the Holy Spirit to dwell in me. That night I felt more peace than I had ever felt. (John 8:36, 2 Corinthians 5:17)
The next morning I woke up with joy, and with the feeling that I had something wonderful to share with the world.
Five weeks later, at the end of January 2012, I got married again.

I tell you that on purpose, because it shows you exactly where I was. I had been set free but I had not been refined. I was still reaching for a person instead of letting Yah finish what He had started in me.

I started a family again, and this time I was getting closer to Yahshua. I was reading my Bible. I was starting to reject the false teachings in the churches I was sitting in. And the closer I got to Him, the more tension it created at home, because I was learning that she did not love Yahshua the way I did.
She was unfaithful in 2015. I tried to forgive it and make the marriage work for the sake of our children and to keep the family together. We separated in August 2016 and eventually divorced.

I had been delivered, but I was still tied to someone who had not been. That soul tie kept me spiritually attached even while I was praying, breaking generational curses, and trying to walk a set apart life. No matter how hard I tried to move forward, I was sabotaged at every turn, and the toxicity created more trauma, more bitterness, and more to forgive. (1 Corinthians 6:16)

sections.heading: LEARNING WHAT I WAS LIVING IN

blocks.v: I did not have a name for what I was living in. I only knew I was confused, and that nothing I did ever fixed anything.

So I started talking to people about my situation. They recognized the signs long before I did. That sent me to studying it, and the more I read, the more I saw my own house on the page. Yah led me through every bit of that. He used other people to open my eyes because I could not see it from the inside.
Most of that season was just me and Yahshua. Praying. Reading. Learning. And He taught me things I never would have chosen to learn.

He taught me how to be silent. That was the hardest one. He taught me I did not have to defend my position every single time it was attacked. Yahshua stood in front of Pilate and would not answer the charges. When He was reviled, He did not revile back. I had spent years trying to explain myself to someone who was never listening. (Matthew 27:12-14, 1 Peter 2:23)
He taught me boundaries. What they are, why they matter, and that putting one up is not unloving. (Proverbs 4:23)
And He showed me what the love bombing actually was. It was not love coming back around. It was manipulation to pull me back under control, every time.
The worst of it was the children being used as a weapon against me. That hurt in a place nothing else reaches.
I had to learn what forgiveness is and what it is not.
Forgiveness was for me. It was how I healed. It was how I put down the bitterness I had been dragging since I was a kid. And it was hard. It was very hard.

But forgiving her never excused what she did, and it was never a reason to stand there and let the abuse keep going. Those are two different things and the enemy loves it when people confuse them. You can release someone completely and still never hand them access to you again.
Forgiving made me stronger. Staying would have made me sick.
The day I was delivered, on the drive home, she told me she was jealous of me.

I did not think much of it then. There were other things after that I did not think much of either. But I have gone back over that season many times since, and I believe the same demon that had been tormenting me went looking for a house and found one. Scripture says an unclean spirit driven out goes through dry places looking for somewhere to go. (Matthew 12:43-45)
I am not guessing at this from a distance. I lived in the middle of it for years, and the attacks have never stopped, not even to this day.
That is why the boundaries stay up. Not because I am bitter. Because the enemy reattaches through any door you leave cracked.
The hardest part of this story is not the drugs or the jail. It is my children.
I am in contact with my oldest from the first marriage. The door is wide open for the other two and always will be, but they have not reached out yet, and I am not going to force it.

After the second marriage ended I tried my best to stay in my two children's lives from that marriage. The manipulation and the hatred aimed at me and at Rebekah made that impossible, and eventually I had to set a boundary and stop communicating with their mother. That boundary cost me contact with them. I told them so myself on the last phone call, almost two years ago now.

I have kept the same phone number since. Same address. Everything about me is public on purpose. When they are old enough to come looking, there will be nothing to find but an open door and a father who is easy to locate.
I pay my child support. I pray for them every single day. I miss them more than I know how to write down.

This is what I mean when I say boundaries cost something. Yah taught me to protect the peace He gave me, and I obeyed Him, and obedience was expensive. I would still obey Him. But I will not pretend it was free. (Isaiah 55:11)
From the separation in August 2016 to the day I married Rebekah was seven years. Those years belonged to Yah.

That was the season He spent refining me. He drew me closer to Him than I had ever been, and He started teaching me His ways and His instructions. He brought me into the Sabbath. He brought me into the feast days. Every layer He pulled off me made the next thing clearer. (1 Peter 1:6-7, Malachi 3:3)
And I was not learning it alone. I had my two children with me for part of that road, and everything Yah was teaching me I turned around and taught them. (Proverbs 22:6)
The week before Passover 2021, I told Yahshua I was all in. No more one foot in and one foot out. I committed my life to His Torah, His instructions, all of it.

I spent that Passover with my children and walked them into this part of the faith for the first time. I do not know what they will hold onto. But they saw their father change in front of them, and I pray that the couple of years they had of that stays in them until the day it matters.
Before He brought her, He made me content without her.

I got to a place where I was settled in my heart about being alone. I told Yahshua straight out in prayer that I was going to live the rest of my life for Him either way. And I told Him that if He did have someone for me, she had to be in the same place in her faith that I was. No compromise on that. I had already lived what happens when you are unequally yoked and call it love. (2 Corinthians 6:14)
About a week after that prayer, Rebekah messaged me.

We had a pile of friends in common, all of them connected to the faith. We started talking, and a week later we met in person on May 11, 2023. That day we happened to drive past a street sign that said TRUELOVE.
We knew. On September 29, 2023, we were married. (Proverbs 18:22)
May 11, 2023. The day we met.

sections.heading: THE GIRL WHO WAS PRAYING FOR A FATHER

blocks.v: Rebekah did not come alone.
Her daughter was eight years old when we met, and she had been praying for a father.

I need you to sit with that for a second. On one side of town there was a man who had been praying for years to be made into a good father, watching his own children get further away from him. On the other side there was an eight year old girl asking Yah for a dad.
He was answering both prayers at the same time, and neither one of us could see it.

She is my daughter. Not a replacement for the ones I am still waiting on, because children are not replaceable and I will never speak about them that way. But she is mine, and Yah gave her to me, and He gave me to her. (Joel 2:25)
Yah did not stop refining us once He put us together. He kept right on removing anything that did not belong in our lives.

We cut out alcohol and unnecessary medicine so we could stay sober minded and keep every demonic door shut and locked. I have not touched alcohol in three years and have not touched marijuana in over a year. We practice forgiveness on purpose, because unforgiveness is one of the enemy's favorite entry points. And we limit anything that can open spiritual doors: music, TV, games, worldly influences, and even certain people.
All of it protects the peace Yah gave us and keeps us walking in the freedom He intended.

sections.heading: WHAT I WANT YOU TO DO WITH THIS

blocks.v: Seek Yahshua with all your heart. Whatever your circumstances look like right now, seek Him. He says that when you search for Him with your whole heart, you will find Him. (Jeremiah 29:13)
He is there even when you are certain He is not. Especially then. (Hebrews 13:5, Psalm 34:18)

Do not give up, and do not hold onto unforgiveness. Forgive, and keep seeking Him, and He will work it all out for your good and for His glory. He works miracles in situations that have no way out. I am one of them. (Romans 8:28)
It takes struggle. It takes tribulation. That is how He refines us into the people He wants us to be. (Isaiah 43:2)

I prayed for years for Yah to make me a good father, a good husband, a set apart man. I could not see that He was already answering that prayer by letting me walk through the fire. And I could not see that while I was praying it, there was a little girl on the other side of town praying for the very thing He was making me into.
I came out refined. Purified. Shaped on the potter's wheel into a vessel He can actually use. (Isaiah 64:8, 2 Timothy 2:21)
If you are in the fire right now, you are not being abandoned. You are being made.
HalleluYah
In the order they appear. WEB, divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai.
"Be angry, and don't sin." Don't let the sun go down on your wrath, neither give place to the devil.
Looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of Elohim, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and many be defiled by it.

His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors until he should pay all that was due to him. So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don't each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.
If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
Therefore if anyone is in Messiah, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
Or don't you know that he who is joined to a prostitute is one body? For, "The two," he says, "will become one flesh."

When he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then Pilate said to him, "Don't you hear how many things they testify against you?" He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
Who, when he was cursed, didn't curse back. When he suffered, didn't threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.
Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

But the unclean spirit, when he is gone out of the man, passes through waterless places, seeking rest, and doesn't find it. Then he says, "I will return into my house from which I came;" and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order. Then he goes and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.
So is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.

Wherein you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials, that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor.
He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
Don't be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship do righteousness and iniquity have? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favor of YHWH.
I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army which I sent among you.
You shall seek me, and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
For he has said, "I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you."
YHWH is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
We know that all things work together for good for those who love Elohim, for those who are called according to his purpose.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
But now, YHWH, you are our Father. We are the clay and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.
If anyone therefore purges himself from these, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, and suitable for the master's use, prepared for every good work.

topics.title: Narcissistic Abuse and Toxic Relationships
topics.subtitle: Know the signs and what Scripture says
topics.lede: If you are in danger right now, the US National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788. Free, confidential, 24 hours a day. The most dangerous moments are when you set a boundary and when you get ready to leave, so make a plan and tell someone safe. Do not do it alone. The rest of this is written so you can name what is happening, because you cannot heal from something you are still calling by the wrong name.

blocks.v: These two words get used as though they mean the same thing, and confusing them keeps people stuck for years.
Toxic is two people caught in unhealthy patterns. Both are contributing something. Both are wounded. Both can grow, if both are willing to look in the mirror. Toxic can be worked on together.

Abusive is one person using fear, control, and punishment to get their way. It is not a pattern between two people. It is a system one person is running on another. Abuse is not a communication problem, and it will not be fixed by trying harder, praying louder, keeping a cleaner house, or being sweeter. You have already tried all of that. It did not work because it was never about you.

blocks.title: The Four Questions
blocks.v: Answer these honestly, even if you have never said the answer out loud. 1. Do you feel afraid? Not afraid of losing them. Afraid of them. If your body braces when you hear their car pull in, your body already knows something your mouth has not admitted yet. 2. Do you walk on eggshells? You rehearse how to say things. You time your words around their mood. That is not being considerate. That is managing a threat.

3. Do you change your behavior to avoid their anger? The friend you stopped seeing. The subject you stopped raising. Each one was traded for a little peace, and the price kept going up. 4. Do you feel smaller every year? Think about who you were when you met them. Abuse rarely takes everything at once. It takes a piece at a time, slow enough that you keep explaining it away.
If you answered yes to these, that is not a rough patch and it is not a season. Naming it is not betrayal. It is the first honest thing you may have done in a long time.
Narcissistic abuse has a playbook, and it is close to the same playbook every time. Once you can name the tactic, it loses a great deal of its power over you.

� Love bombing. Overwhelming affection, gifts, and talk of soulmates within weeks. It is not love. It is a hook. � Gaslighting. You are told it never happened, you remember it wrong, you are too sensitive. Over time you stop trusting your own mind. Projection. Everything they are doing gets accused of you. The liar calls you a liar. The unfaithful one accuses you of unfaithfulness.
� Blame shifting. Their rage, their job, their choices, their sin. Every problem they have becomes your fault, until you are the reason for everything.

� DARVO. Deny, attack, and reverse victim and offender. You raise something they did, and within two minutes you are apologizing and they are the wounded one. Silent treatment. Punishment dressed up as needing space. You are frozen out until you come back on their terms.

� Hoovering. When you start pulling away, the charm comes back. Tears, promises, the person you first fell for. It lasts exactly as long as it takes to get you back. Future faking. Promises of the thing you want most. The wedding, the move, the change, the counseling. It is always coming and it never arrives.

� Triangulation. A third person is pulled in to compare you to, compete with, or report on you. You end up managing a relationship that is not yours. Smear campaign. Your reputation is rewritten before you ever get to speak. By the time you tell your side, people have already been told what to think of you.
� Reactive abuse and baiting. You are pushed until you finally snap, and then your reaction becomes the evidence that you were the problem all along.
� Cruelty as a joke. The remark that cuts, followed by telling you that you cannot take a joke. It is contempt with an escape hatch attached.

An abuser rarely works alone for long. Family, friends, coworkers, and sometimes church people get recruited to carry the message, apply pressure, report back on you, and tell you that you are overreacting.

Some of them know exactly what they are doing. Most have no idea they are being used. That distinction matters when you are deciding who is dangerous and who is simply deceived, but it does not change what you need to do in the moment. You do not owe anyone your story just because they came asking for it on someone else's behalf.

This is also where the smear campaign does its real work. The account of you that reaches people is not yours. Do not spend your strength trying to correct every version of it. The people who matter will watch your life over time and draw the right conclusion.
This is the one that does damage nothing else can reach, because it puts the abuse in YHWH's mouth. Scripture stops being bread and becomes a weapon.
Submission preached one direction. Verses about your role are quoted constantly. The verses about theirs are never mentioned.

� Your walk used as leverage. If you do not do what they want, you are told you are not right with YHWH, you are rebellious, you are in sin, you need to pray more. Prayer withheld. They will not pray with you, will not pray over the home, and then hold your spiritual life up as the thing that is lacking. Forgiveness weaponized. You are told that forgiving means forgetting, staying quiet, and letting it continue. That is not forgiveness. That is a leash with a Bible verse on it.
� Repentance performed. Tears and apologies arrive on schedule, especially when you get close to leaving. Nothing about the behavior changes afterward.
� Leaders enlisted. Counsel is sought only where the story has already been told their way, so the correction always lands on you.

Hear this plainly. Shame that is manufactured by another person is not conviction from YHWH. Conviction is specific, it is aimed at something you actually did, and it leads you toward repentance and freedom. Manufactured shame is vague, it is aimed at who you are, and it leads you toward compliance. One sets you free. The other keeps you useful.

In the last days grievous times will come. For men will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, without natural affection, unforgiving, slanderers, without self control, fierce, not lovers of good, traitors, headstrong, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, holding a form of godliness but having denied its power. Turn away from these also.

Early on you were invited to open up. The childhood you survived. The mistakes you made before you knew better. The thing you had never told anyone. It felt like intimacy. For some people it is intimacy. For an abuser it is inventory.

Later, every one of those things comes back at you as ammunition. Your past is quoted to prove you cannot be trusted now. A mistake you repented of years ago is produced in the middle of an argument that has nothing to do with it. The wound you were most afraid to name is used to explain why your objection does not count.

There is a mark of the enemy on this one. Revelation calls him the accuser. Accusation is the constant recitation of what you have already been forgiven for. If someone in your life is doing that work full time, you are entitled to notice whose work it is.
There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Messiah Yahshua.
When the usual pressure stops working, the children become the pressure. It shows up in ways that are easy to deny and devastating to live under.
� Threats about custody. You are told you will lose them, that no court will believe you, that you have nothing without them.
� Children as messengers. They are sent to deliver what the adult will not say directly, or sent back to report what you said.
� Turning them against you. Your character is worked on quietly, in the car, at bedtime, until your own child repeats a phrase that is not theirs.
� The good parent performance. Sudden, visible involvement whenever there is an audience, and none at all when there is not.
� Guilt through the children. Everything you consider doing for your own safety is reframed as something you would be doing to them.

If this is where you are, write things down. Dates, what was said, what was witnessed. Not to build a case against a person, but because your memory will be worked on and you will need something outside yourself that tells the truth. Keep it somewhere they cannot reach.

sections.heading: 7. The Ladder and the Boiling Frog

blocks.v: It almost never starts loud. It escalates slowly, and the slowness is the point.

blocks.title: Stage What It Looks Like
blocks.v: Small dismissals. You are too sensitive. You are imagining it. 1

items: Gaslighting. You are told it never happened. 2
Verbal abuse. Name calling, mocking, yelling meant to dominate. 3
Intimidation. Slammed doors, broken things, blocked exits. 4
Coercive control. Money, time, and decisions stop being yours. 5
Physical violence, or the threat of it. 6
The honeymoon reset. Tears, gifts, promises, and then it begins again. 7

blocks.v: That last stage is not repentance. That is the cycle catching its breath.

This is the boiling frog. A joke that stings. A phone that gets checked. A friend you slowly stop seeing. By the time it gets loud, your support system is already gone and your sense of normal has been quietly rewritten. That is why people on the outside ask why you did not leave at the beginning. There was no beginning. There was a hundred small beginnings, each one small enough to excuse.
Scripture does not instruct you to fix these people. It instructs you to guard yourself, and it names the behavior for what it is.

Now the deeds of the flesh are obvious, which are sexual immorality, uncleanness, lustfulness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, strife, jealousies, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these.
Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment.
Have no fellowship with the unfruitful deeds of darkness, but rather even reprove them.
Read 1 John 4:18 again. Love and the fear of punishment cannot live in the same house. Whatever is producing that fear in you, it is not love.

And notice what 2 Timothy does after the list. It does not say fix them. It says turn away. Boundaries are not rebellion, and they are not a failure of faith. Boundaries protect what YHWH entrusted to you.

sections.heading: 9. Leaving, and Where to Find Help

blocks.title: Read This Part Carefully
blocks.v: The most dangerous moments are when you set a boundary, when you stand up, and when you get ready to leave. That is when the control feels threatened. Make a plan. Tell someone safe. Do not do it alone.

US National Domestic Violence Hotline. 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788. Free, confidential, available 24 hours a day. They will help you build a safety plan, and you do not have to be ready to leave to call them.

Celebrate Recovery. A Christ centered recovery program, and not only for addiction. Two thirds of the people in those rooms are there for something else: codependency, control issues, anxiety, depression, growing up in a broken home, and emotional, mental, physical, and sexual abuse. You do not register, you do not pay, and you do not have to tell anyone you are coming.

blocks.title: Resource Where To Find It
blocks.v: crlocator.com Find a group

items: celebraterecovery.com/weekly-online-recovery-meetings Free weekly online meeting
crgroups.info Find your local CR representative
app.kingdom-life-ministry.com Kingdom Life Study app

blocks.v: One thing to hold on to. Celebrate Recovery is a healing community, not a safety plan. If you are still living in the house with an active abuser, the hotline comes first. CR is where the healing work happens once you are safe enough to do it.
And if you take nothing else from this: the shame you are carrying was handed to you. It was never yours. You can set it down.

blocks.title: Passage Why It Is Here Where
blocks.v: The deeds of the flesh named plainly Section 8 Galatians 5:19 to 21

items: The character described, and the instruction to turn away Section 4 2 Timothy 3:1 to 5
Guard your heart, for out of it is the wellspring of life Section 8 Proverbs 4:23
Perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment Section 8 1 John 4:18
No fellowship with the unfruitful deeds of darkness Section 8 Ephesians 5:11
No condemnation for those in Messiah Yahshua Section 5 Romans 8:1
The accuser of the brothers, and what accusation looks like Section 5 Revelation 12:10
YHWH is near to those who have a broken heart Closing Psalm 34:18
