topics.title: Real Deliverance Is Impossible Without Forgiveness
topics.subtitle: Forgiveness, the Root of Deliverance
topics.note: A Teaching Study on Forgiveness in the Kingdom Life Scripture quoted from the World English Bible, divine name rendered YHWH, Elohim, and Adonai. Torah is referred to throughout as the instructions of YHWH.

blocks.title: The Heart Of It
blocks.v: Deliverance is not just about getting something dark out of you. It is about letting YHWH take something heavy off of you. At the root of that is forgiveness.

You cannot walk in lasting freedom while you are still holding the chains of unforgiveness in your own hands. You can cast out the fruit all day long. If the root stays in the ground, the fruit comes back.
This teaching is not a theory for us. It is the ground I was delivered on.

I grew up with a wonderful mother who took me to church and taught me the things of YHWH. But I carried pain and unforgiveness in my heart from growing up in a divorced and broken home, and that unforgiveness did not stay quiet. It turned into bitterness, the bitterness opened doors, and those doors led me into gangs, jail, drugs, alcohol, and destructive relationships. Deep down I always wanted to do what was right. I just did not know demons were influencing me.

The weekend of December 22, 2011, I attended an Encounter at Tarpley, a three day deliverance event. The first two days were not about demons at all. They were about forgiveness. We prayed, and we wrote down the traumas and hidden hurts so we could forgive the people who wounded us. I asked YHWH to show me the unforgiveness buried in my heart, and He brought up things I did not even remember. I wrote letters, and I forgave people I had been holding for years.

By the third day He had already shown me that the root of everything was unforgiveness. When the pastor commanded the spirit to come out and I breathed out, I felt something leave my body. I declared Yahshua as my Lord and Savior right there, and that night I felt more peace than I had ever known. The deliverance came after the forgiveness, not before it. That order is the whole message of this study.

blocks.title: What I Learned The Hard Way
blocks.v: Being delivered once did not mean I was done forgiving. The years after brought new wounds, new betrayals, and more to forgive. Forgiveness was not one prayer at an altar. It became a way of life, and it still is. Rebekah and I practice forgiveness on purpose, because unforgiveness is one of the enemy's favorite entry points. The full story is in my testimony handout.
Many believers think of deliverance only as casting out demons. Biblically it is broader than that: rescue out of bondage, spiritual, emotional, and sometimes physical, into the freedom of Messiah.
who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love;
Deliverance is a transfer of kingdoms, not only a moment of manifestation. It is a change of address in the spirit. It can happen in a moment, and it is also walked out over a lifetime.

The Spirit of Adonai is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed,
The Same Word for Release and Forgiveness

Look at the word release in that verse. In Greek it is aphesis, and it appears twice: release to the captives, and deliver, literally send away in release, those who are crushed. That is the same noun the New Testament uses for the forgiveness of sins. In Ephesians 1:7 we have redemption through His blood, the aphesis of our trespasses. In Luke 24:47, repentance and aphesis of sins is to be preached to all the nations.

When Yahshua stood up in Nazareth and announced His mission, He used the forgiveness word to describe deliverance. In His mouth they are not two different ministries. Release from sin and release from bondage come out of the same word.

blocks.title: The Torah Behind It
blocks.v: Yahshua was reading Isaiah 61:1, proclaim liberty to the captives. The Hebrew word for liberty is deror, the same word YHWH used for the Jubilee: proclaim liberty throughout the land (Leviticus 25:10). When the Torah was translated into Greek before Yahshua's time, the translators used this same word, aphesis, for the Jubilee and for the seventh year release of debts (Leviticus 25:10; Deuteronomy 15:1-2). Deliverance, forgiveness, and the cancelling of debts all come out of one picture in YHWH's instructions: the year when every debt is released and every captive goes home.
Before we can walk in forgiveness, we need to know what Scripture actually means by it. nasa (Hebrew)
To lift, to carry, to bear away. Forgiveness pictured as a weight lifted off and carried somewhere else. Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven (Psalm 32:1). salach (Hebrew)
To pardon. In the Tanakh this verb only ever has YHWH as its subject. Full pardon belongs to Him (Jeremiah 31:34; compare Psalm 130:4). kaphar (Hebrew)
To cover, to make atonement. The word behind Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:30). aphiemi (Greek)
To send away, to let go, to release, to cancel a debt. The main word for forgive in the Gospels. Forgive us our debts (Matthew 6:12). aphesis (Greek)
Release, liberty, forgiveness. Used for both the forgiveness of sins and the release of captives (Luke 4:18; Ephesians 1:7). charizomai (Greek)
To give freely, from charis, grace. Forgiveness handed out as a gift, not earned (Ephesians 4:32; Colossians 2:13; 3:13). apoluo (Greek)
To loose, to set free. Set free, and you will be set free (Luke 6:37). opheilema (Greek)
A debt, something owed. Yahshua taught us to call sin a debt (Matthew 6:12; compare Luke 11:4).
Put them together and the picture is clear. Forgiveness is not a warm feeling. It is lifting a weight off, cancelling a debt, and sending the case away to the only One who has the right to pardon.

sections.heading: Forgiveness Was Always in the Instructions

blocks.v: Some people think forgiveness is a New Testament idea that replaced a harsh Old Testament. That is not what the Torah says. Forgiveness is written into YHWH's own name and into His instructions to His people.

YHWH! YHWH, a merciful and gracious Elohim, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and that will by no means clear the guilty,
Notice both halves. He forgives, and He does not pretend sin is nothing. Forgiveness in Scripture never calls evil good. It releases the debt while still calling it a debt.

You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him. You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am YHWH.

Yahshua quoted the end of this passage as the second great commandment (Matthew 22:39). Read the whole thing and you find a full teaching on forgiveness in the Torah itself: do not hate in your heart, speak the truth plainly when you are wronged, do not take revenge, and do not carry a grudge. Honest confrontation and heart release live side by side. The instructions never asked you to pretend you were not hurt. They told you not to keep it.
The Year of Release

Every seventh year YHWH commanded Israel to release the debts owed by a neighbor and brother (Deuteronomy 15:1-2). Every fiftieth year the Jubilee proclaimed liberty through the whole land, and people went home to their inheritance (Leviticus 25:10). Debt was never meant to be carried forever in YHWH's kingdom. When Yahshua taught us to pray forgive us our debts, He was not inventing something new. He was speaking the language of His Father's instructions.
Joseph
Joseph's brothers sold him into slavery. Years later, with the power of Egypt in his hand, he could have done anything to them.

Joseph said to them, "Don't be afraid, for am I in the place of Elohim? As for you, you meant evil against me, but Elohim meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive. Now therefore don't be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones." He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

Am I in the place of Elohim? That is forgiveness in one question. Joseph refused to sit in the judge's seat. He named the evil plainly, you meant evil against me, and he handed the verdict to YHWH. Joseph also tested his brothers before he revealed himself to them (Genesis 42-44). Forgiveness and wisdom walked together in him.

Scripture uses courtroom language for the spiritual realm. Satan is called the accuser of our brothers, who accuses them before our Elohim day and night (Revelation 12:10). The Greek word is kategor, a legal accuser, a prosecutor. Yahshua is our Advocate with the Father (1 John 2:1). YHWH is the righteous Judge (Psalm 7:11). And the record of our debt is called a cheirographon, a handwritten certificate of debt, an IOU signed in our own hand (Colossians 2:14).
That is why we speak about legal ground. The phrase itself is not in Scripture, but the courtroom is, and the enemy works like a prosecutor looking for any right to stay.
"Be angry, and don't sin." Don't let the sun go down on your wrath, neither give place to the devil.
Place is the Greek topos: a place, a room, an opening, an opportunity. Anger held past sunset hands the devil a place to stand. Unforgiveness is like a landing pad in the spirit.
Two Places You Can Give
Paul uses the exact same phrase, give place, in Romans 12.
Don't seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to Elohim's wrath. For it is written, "Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says Adonai."

Every wound leaves you holding a place. You will give it to someone. Either you give place to Elohim's judgment and let Him repay, or you keep the case open in your own heart and give place to the devil. Forgiveness is choosing which one gets the room.
For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Messiah, that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan; for we are not ignorant of his schemes.

This is the clearest verse in Scripture tying forgiveness to spiritual warfare. Paul forgave so that Satan would not gain an advantage. Unforgiveness is not only a relationship problem. It is one of the enemy's schemes.

blocks.title: The Lease
blocks.v: Trying to do deliverance without forgiveness is like trying to evict a tenant who is still holding a valid, signed lease. You can shout at him all day. He will show you the paper. Forgiveness cancels the lease. Then the command to leave has nothing standing against it.
looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of Elohim, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and many be defiled by it;

The writer of Hebrews is reaching back to the Torah. In Deuteronomy 29:18, Moses warned Israel against a root that produces bitter poison and wormwood, a heart turning away from YHWH. A root is hidden underground. Nobody sees it. What they see is what it produces.

Most people fight the fruit. They want anger cast out, depression cast out, fear cast out. Those may be real spirits, and they may really need to go. But if the root of bitterness is still in the ground, the fruit comes back next season. You can pick apples off a tree all day. If the roots are healthy, more apples are coming. We have to go underground.
How the Root Grows

Paul lists the progression in a single verse. Offense becomes lingering anger. Anger becomes resentment. Resentment hardens into bitterness. Bitterness becomes a hard heart, and a hard heart becomes an open door.

Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, outcry, and slander be put away from you, with all malice. And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as Elohim also in Messiah forgave you.
It Defiles Many

Bitterness is never a private sin. It spreads into your marriage, your children, your ministry, and your family line. Children pick up a parent's bitterness long before they can name it. Whole families go generations without speaking, carrying grudges nobody remembers the start of, living under a heaviness they think is just their personality.
I know this one personally. I came out of a broken home carrying pain that was not mine to begin with, and it opened doors in my life before I was old enough to understand them.
Peter asked Yahshua how many times he should forgive a brother who sins against him, and offered seven as a generous number. Yahshua answered:
I don't tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.

The Greek phrase can be read seventy times seven or seventy seven times. Either way, Yahshua is not handing Peter a number to count to. The same Greek phrase appears in the old Greek translation of Genesis 4:24, where Lamech boasted that if Cain would be avenged seven times, Lamech would be avenged seventy seven times. Lamech measured vengeance without limit. Yahshua turns it around and measures forgiveness without limit.
The Size of the Debt

In the parable that follows, the servant owed ten thousand talents. One talent was about six thousand denarii, and a denarius was about a day's wage for a laborer. Ten thousand talents is around sixty million days of work, well over one hundred fifty thousand years of wages. It was a debt no one could ever repay. His fellow servant owed him one hundred denarii, a few months of work. A real debt, but next to what he had just been forgiven, almost nothing.
Yahshua is not saying what was done to you was small. He is saying what you were forgiven is bigger.

Then his lord called him in, and said to him, "You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt, because you begged me. Shouldn't you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?" His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him. So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don't each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.
Who the Tormentors Are

The Greek word is basanistes, a torturer or jailer, the officer who pressed a prisoner for what was owed. Notice who hands the servant over: his master. And Yahshua says plainly, so my heavenly Father will also do to you. This is first a sober warning about the Father's judgment, and we should hear it that way before anything else.

It also describes what many believers are living under right now: anxiety, mental torment, replaying the offense at night, a heart that never rests. Since Paul says twice that unforgiveness gives the devil a place and an advantage (Ephesians 4:27; 2 Corinthians 2:11), it is fair to see tormenting spirits at work in that torment. You can pray, fast, and go to every service, and if you are still holding someone in your heart, you are handing the enemy a right to harass you.

blocks.title: From Your Hearts
blocks.v: Verse 35 says from your hearts. Yahshua is not asking for words spoken at an altar while you keep the file open. He is also not asking you to feel warm toward the person first. It is a real decision, made sincerely, that reaches all the way down. Sometimes you walk it down there one day at a time.

Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors... For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you don't forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

Of every line in the prayer Yahshua taught, this is the only one He stopped to explain afterward. That should tell us how seriously He means it. We forgive because we have been forgiven an infinite debt, and our forgiveness of others is the evidence that we actually received the Father's mercy.
Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone; so that your Father, who is in heaven, may also forgive you your transgressions.

Yahshua ties forgiveness to prayer itself. Whenever you stand praying. Before you ask for healing, breakthrough, or deliverance, He sends you back to your own heart to check who you are still holding.
Don't judge, and you won't be judged. Don't condemn, and you won't be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.
Set free, and you will be set free. That is deliverance language in Yahshua's own mouth, and He connects your freedom to the freedom you give.
Forgiveness and Healing

Scripture connects the heart and the body. David said that when he kept silent about his own sin, his bones wasted away, until he confessed and YHWH forgave (Psalm 32:3-5). A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones (Proverbs 17:22). James ties confession and prayer for one another directly to healing (James 5:16).
We do not promise that forgiving someone will heal every sickness. We do say this: bitterness is poison to the whole person, and when the poison comes out, the wound can finally close.

sections.heading: Pride, the Root Under the Root

blocks.v: Here is something YHWH has shown us, and we hold it as a conviction: pride is the root of unforgiveness, and humility is the root of forgiveness. Scripture does not say it in that exact sentence, but look how it pairs them.

Put on therefore, as Elohim's chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance; bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Messiah forgave you, so you also do.

Humility is put on first, and forgiveness follows. Ephesians walks the same road: it opens with walk in all lowliness and humility (Ephesians 4:2) and arrives at forgiving each other (Ephesians 4:32).

Pride is sneaky. It rarely calls itself pride. It says: what they did was too big. I have a right to hold this. They have to come to me first. I am just protecting myself. I forgave them, I just cannot let it go. Look at the unforgiving servant again. He had just been released from a debt of millions, and he walked out and grabbed his fellow servant by the throat over a hundred denarii (Matthew 18:28). He received mercy without ever being humbled by it.
But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, "Elohim resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble."

blocks.title: The Order Of Things
blocks.v: Humility is the root of forgiveness. Forgiveness is the root of deliverance.
If you are stuck and cannot forgive, do not start by trying harder to forgive. Start by humbling yourself before YHWH. Grace goes to the humble, and grace is what makes forgiveness possible.
Many people will not forgive because they think forgiveness means something it does not. Clear these away and the door opens.
Not a feeling
It is a decision of the will, often repeated. You can still hurt and truly forgive. Feelings usually catch up to obedience over time.
Not saying it was okay
YHWH forgives and still will by no means clear the guilty (Exodus 34:7). Joseph said, you meant evil against me (Genesis 50:20). Forgiveness names the sin and releases the debt.
Not forgetting
When YHWH says He will not remember our sins (Isaiah 43:25; Jeremiah 31:34), it means He will not hold them against us, not that He has amnesia. You can remember and still not collect.
Not reconciliation

Reconciliation takes two people and real repentance (Luke 17:3; Matthew 18:15-17). Forgiveness takes you and YHWH. Whenever you stand praying, forgive (Mark 11:25). You can forgive fully and still have no contact.
Not trust or access

Paul released Alexander the coppersmith to Adonai's repayment and still warned Timothy to beware of him (2 Timothy 4:14-15). Do not befriend a hot tempered man, lest you learn his ways (Proverbs 22:24-25). Forgiveness is given. Trust is rebuilt by fruit over time.
Not removing

Forgiveness cancels your personal right to revenge. It does not cancel the law of the land or the consequences duty to protect others. Justice belongs to YHWH and to the authorities He has set in place (Romans 12:19; 13:1-4).
Not staying silent
The same Torah that forbids grudges commands honest rebuke (Leviticus 19:17). Forgiveness never requires you to stay quiet about abuse.

My own story taught me this one the hard way. Forgiving never excused what was done, and it was never a reason to stand there and let the abuse keep going. You can release someone completely and still never hand them access to you again. That boundary has cost me more than I can put on paper, and I would still obey. Forgiving made me stronger. Staying would have made me sick.
Two Ways to Carry a Wound
Unforgiveness
Holds the debt, rehearses the pain, partners with the accuser, and leads to torment.
Forgiveness
Cancels the debt, hands the pain to YHWH, partners with mercy, and leads to peace.
Soulish deliverance
Emotional hype and momentary relief, with no heart level release.
True deliverance
Root level forgiveness, renouncing agreement with darkness, and an ongoing walk in mercy.
Self protection
I will not forgive, so I will not get hurt again.
YHWH's protection
I forgive, I set boundaries, and I trust YHWH to be my defender and my healer.

sections.heading: Forgiving When They Never Say Sorry

blocks.v: What if they never apologize? What if they are not sorry at all? What if they are no longer alive? Yahshua forgave while He was still being wronged.
Yahshua said, "Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing."

An honest note for the careful student: some of the oldest manuscripts of Luke do not include this sentence, which is why many Bibles footnote it. The same heart stands on solid ground without it. Stephen, with the stones still flying, cried out, Adonai, don't hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60). And Peter says of Yahshua:
who, when he was cursed, didn't curse back. When he suffered, didn't threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously;

Committed Himself to Him who judges righteously. Forgiveness does not wait for the offender. Reconciliation does. You can forgive someone who never apologizes, never changes, and is no longer alive, because forgiveness is settled between you and YHWH. You are not declaring them innocent. You are moving the case to His court.

sections.heading: We Forgive Because We Were Forgiven

blocks.v: You were dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh. He made you alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, wiping out the handwriting in ordinances which was against us. He has taken it out of the way, nailing it to the cross. Having stripped the principalities and the powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it.

This is the victory ground. At the cross Yahshua did not only defeat demons. He cancelled our debt. He took the handwritten record that stood against us and nailed it to the cross, and in the very next breath Paul says He stripped the principalities and powers. Notice the order: first the debt is cancelled, then the powers are disarmed. The accuser's weapon was the record of debt. Once it was nailed to the cross, he had nothing left to hold over us.
That is the pattern for every deliverance. Cancel the debt first. Then the powers lose their grip.
Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.

The people who struggle most to forgive are often the ones who have not yet let YHWH's forgiveness sink all the way into them. When you finally see the size of what you were released from, the hundred denarii someone owes you starts to look different.

And the accuser is defeated the same way every time: they overcame him because of the Lamb's blood, and because of the word of their testimony (Revelation 12:11). The blood that cancelled the debt, and people willing to stand up and tell what it did for them.

sections.heading: When You Are the One Who Needs Forgiveness

blocks.v: If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and remember there that your brother has anything against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

Forgiveness runs both directions. Yahshua cared so much about this that He told people to walk away from the altar in the middle of an offering to go make it right. Ask forgiveness specifically. Not I am sorry if you were hurt. Name what you did, own it, and ask. Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed (James 5:16).

Then receive YHWH's forgiveness for yourself. If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness (1 John 1:9). Scripture never actually tells us to forgive ourselves. It tells us to receive His forgiveness and stop overruling His verdict. If the Judge has cancelled the debt, you do not get to keep collecting it from yourself.

sections.heading: Walking It Out: Six Steps to Freedom

blocks.v: This is the same path I walked at the Encounter, and the one we walk with people now. Do it slowly. Do it out loud.
Invite the Ruach to search your heart. Do not rely on your memory. Rely on His light. Ask Him, Ruach HaKodesh,
who am I still holding? Faces, names, and memories will come up, some you had forgotten. That is where He wants to begin. (Psalm 139:23-24)
Name the hurt honestly. Do not say it is fine. Say what they did and how it affected you. Write it down if you need to. I
wrote letters. Truth telling is part of healing. (Psalm 62:8; Leviticus 19:17)
Release the debt. Say it out loud: In the name of Yahshua, I choose to forgive [name] for [what they did]. I release them
from the debt. I cancel my demand for an apology. I hand this case to You, Righteous Judge. This is an act of your will, whether or not the feelings are there yet. (Matthew 18:35; Romans 12:19)
Renounce the foothold. Once the debt is cancelled, the enemy has no legal right left. In the name of Yahshua, I
renounce bitterness, resentment, hatred, and every spirit that came in through this unforgiveness. You have no more right here. Leave now. (Ephesians 4:27; James 4:7)
Ask to be filled. Do not leave the house empty. An unclean spirit that is driven out goes looking for its old house, and if
it finds it empty, it comes back with seven worse (Matthew 12:43-45). Ask YHWH to fill that place with His love, His peace, and His truth. (John 14:27; Romans 5:5)
Set boundaries and keep forgiving. Freedom requires walking in wisdom. Guard your heart (Proverbs 4:23) and close
the doors that let it in. When the old offense comes back to mind, forgive again, seventy times seven, until the memory has no hook left in it.
Pray this out loud. Put the real names in. Take your time.

blocks.title: Pray It Out Loud
blocks.v: Father YHWH, in the name of Yahshua, I come before You now. Search me and know my heart. Show me every place I am still holding unforgiveness, even the things I have forgotten. I choose right now to forgive [name] for [what they did]. I release them from the debt they owe me. I cancel my demand for an apology, for repayment, and for revenge. I give this case to You, Righteous Judge. I give place to Your judgment, and I give no place to the devil. I renounce bitterness, resentment, hatred, anger, and every spirit that entered through this unforgiveness. In the name of Yahshua, you have no more legal right here. Leave now. Yahshua, I receive Your forgiveness for my own sin, and I stop collecting a debt You already cancelled. Fill every empty place in me with Your Ruach, Your love, Your peace, and Your truth. Give me wisdom to walk in boundaries and grace to keep forgiving. Thank You for nailing my debt to the cross. I have been set free, and I will set others free. In the name of Yahshua. Amen.
